title: iliria Performance Theory
principle: **iliria Performance Principle #1** — Benchmarks, committed artifacts, and machine-generated reports are authoritative. Conversation, summaries, and status updates are not. If they disagree, the artifact wins.
intro: This is the permanent hypothesis → prediction → measurement → status map for every optimization this project has tried on the M5 Max streamed-MoE engine (GLM-5.2 744B, int4, disk-streamed experts). **New contributors: check here before proposing an optimization** — most ideas in this space have already been measured, and a surprising number of "obviously good" ones (bigger static pin, more prefetch, continuous batching, self-speculation) are dead on this specific workload for specific, measured reasons. Read the Notes line before re-proposing.

Every entry is built only from committed records — internal-findings entries, this repo's own `docs/*.md`, this repo's own README, and gate-commit messages — never from conversation or an in-flight status update. Where two committed sources disagreed, that is called out explicitly rather than silently resolved (see also the `source_conflicts` list in the source JSON).

entries.name: MTP speculative decoding (streamed path)

regime.context: 112-token pin trials / overnight coding-profile sweep; pre-DSA, pre-Metal-prefill-kernel (has_dsa=false throughout)
regime.cache: default adaptive LRU, no static pin
regime.backend: CPU

entries.hypothesis: GLM-5.2's native multi-token-prediction (MTP) draft head, verified in batch, speeds up decode by accepting multiple tokens per forward pass.
entries.prediction: None recorded numerically ahead of the M5 Max streamed-engine test.

measurements.display: DRAFT=0: 1.49 tok/s; DRAFT=2: 0.37 tok/s; DRAFT=4: 0.28 tok/s.
measurements.source: internal findings, not staged 'MTP results'; reconfirmed same-session internal findings, not staged #30

measurements.display: Overnight coding-profile sweep with acceptance instrumented: DRAFT=1 86% acceptance but only 0.49 tok/s; DRAFT=2 54% acceptance, 0.58 tok/s; DRAFT=4 27% acceptance, 0.44 tok/s — all below DRAFT=0's 1.44 tok/s. High acceptance did not compensate for the larger union of routed experts verification loads.
measurements.source: internal findings, not staged

entries.notes: Regime-specific, not a blanket MTP verdict: internal findings, not staged #4 verified ~90% draft acceptance for a grafted MTP head on a different (unpruned, non-streamed) model/project, and internal findings, not staged #13 separately measured 0% acceptance on a pruned GLM-5.2 (router mismatch) — three different MTP outcomes across three different projects/regimes, each internally consistent once the regime is named; not a contradiction. internal findings, not staged #27 flags this kill as measured before the Metal prefill kernel and DSA indexer existed and marks it owed one cheap 'graveyard revival' probe under the new physics — not yet run as of the latest committed record. Root-cause mechanism (why K-token verification cancels the gain on a memory-bandwidth-bound MoE): internal findings, not staged #13.

entries.name: Sketch-draft self-speculative decoding

regime.context: N/A — feasibility study, no live engine run
regime.cache: proposed 30GB int8 sketch store vs. today's 97GB expert cache
regime.backend: CPU (proposed, not built)

entries.hypothesis: Keeping low-rank (int8, rank 31–84) sketches of all 19,200 routed experts resident in RAM, drafting K tokens per round on sketches alone (zero disk), then verifying with one batched exact forward whose batch-union MoE reads each unique routed expert once, lets accepted tokens amortize disk bytes and break the disk-bytes-per-token ceiling toward 2x.
entries.prediction: None recorded numerically pre-study. The study derives that breakeven needs per-token acceptance ≥0.70, the roadmap's +15% gate needs ≥0.80, and predicts a best case of ~1.4x against a 2x bar (the sketch-draft feasibility analysis).

measurements.display: Miss bytes per drafted token are flat in K (~3.6 GB at K=1, 2, 4, 8, 12) — the batch-union shrinks unique experts per token (8→4.8 at K=8) but only dedupes requests that were already LRU hits (routing is near-memoryless: mean top-8 Jaccard 0.18 at lag 1, decaying to 0.07 at lag 16). Disk bytes per emitted token are ≥K/(K+1) of today even at 100% acceptance, and ≥1.1x today once a 30 GB sketch store is honestly charged against the expert cache (97→67 GB, −8.4 hit points, +27% miss bytes).
measurements.source: the sketch-draft feasibility analysis §§1–3

entries.notes: MTP's live 4x loss (previous entry) is the measured precedent for the same verify economics. Acceptance ≥0.8 from a ~1.5–4%-of-full-rank sketch on a 744B model sitting near argmax ties is 'the study's least plausible assumption, and the one thing offline math cannot decide' (the sketch-draft feasibility analysis §5). A cheap two-stage empirical gate (one-layer reconstruction probe, then teacher-forced top-1 agreement ≥0.8) is specified but not run; must pass before any engine work starts. Cross-referenced in internal findings, not staged #52 and internal findings, not staged #33's verdict table.

entries.name: Static pinning / hotset training

regime.context: 112 tokens (pin-scaling trials); 24-prompt coding hotset training
regime.cache: static/pinned hot-set, 23.5–48.9GB sizes
regime.backend: CPU

entries.hypothesis: A larger static/pinned expert hot-set, or one trained from a more diverse prompt history, concentrates the expert distribution enough to raise cache hit rate — and therefore throughput — toward an implicit ~85–90% target.
entries.prediction: None recorded numerically; the implicit hope was that bigger/better-trained pins would approach the 85–90% hit-rate region (internal findings, not staged, 'Current decision').

measurements.display: Pin scaling (3 trials/mode, 112 tokens): 23.5 GB pin (1,240 experts) → 66.2% hit, 1.43 tok/s; 46.9 GB (2,480 experts) → 69.9% hit, 1.32 tok/s; 48.9 GB (2,584 experts) → 70.3% hit, 1.36 tok/s — hit rate rose but throughput fell, because larger pins steal adaptive-LRU capacity and add Metal dispatch overhead.
measurements.source: internal findings, not staged #30

measurements.display: 24-prompt coding hotset training: expert-layer coverage rose 69→95.8% (more diffuse, not less); top-32/layer coverage fell 54.5%→40.8%.
measurements.source: internal findings, not staged #47; internal findings, not staged 'Overnight coding profile'

entries.notes: The distribution is fundamentally flat for this MoE on a coding workload — diverse prompts broaden it rather than concentrate it. Would only flip if a workload were found whose expert distribution is genuinely Pareto-heavy (the offline math-verdict record Study 2 independently confirms routing is diffuse: top 10% of experts carry only ~35–38% of mass). Lever redirected to router-lookahead prediction instead (PILOT K6, next entries).

entries.name: Bomb / Shotgun bulk-prewarming prefetch

regime.context: 96,000 route records, coding profile
regime.cache: global (Bomb) vs. layer-local (Shotgun) frequency-ranked prewarm
regime.backend: CPU (offline sim only)

entries.hypothesis: Prediction-free bulk prewarming (Bomb: load top-K most-frequent experts for all layers each interval) or a spread limited to nearby layers (Shotgun) raises hit rate as well as router-guided prefetch, without needing a router signal.
entries.prediction: None recorded numerically ahead of the offline simulation.

measurements.display: Bomb K=8 → 57.5% hit (−5.9 pts vs no-prefetch's 63.4%); K=32 → 55.6% (−7.8 pts); K=64 → 36.3% (−27.1 pts, catastrophic). Shotgun's best simulated config (K=64) reached 73.1% hit — better than Bomb but still well below PILOT K6's real-run 80.6%.
measurements.source: internal findings, not staged #46; internal findings, not staged 'Shotgun and Bomb simulations'

entries.notes: The more you bomb, the more useful LRU entries you evict — frequency-ranked guesses don't match the temporal access pattern a cache depends on. Ranking: PILOT (router-guided) > Shotgun (layer-local frequency) > Bomb (global frequency) > no prefetch at high K.

entries.name: PILOT K6 router-lookahead prefetch

regime.context: k6-matrix-20260714-090059, 3 held-out prompts × 3 rotated trials
regime.cache: frozen .fa_usage usage profile, hash-gated
regime.backend: CPU attention + LRU expert cache

entries.hypothesis: Using the router's post-attention state at layer N to predict which experts layer N+1 will need, and loading them into the LRU ahead of the matmul, raises cache hit rate and, by extension, decode throughput.
entries.prediction: Initial single-prompt A/B recorded '+11 hit points, byte-exact, +0.29% throughput' (commit 896adb1), later shown to be a masked, noise-level neutral result.

measurements.display: (a) Hit-rate / prediction quality, held-out matrix, hashes clean: +13.1 to +13.4 hit points on every prompt, live hit rate (77.8–79.5%) sitting at the Belady offline ceiling for this trace family (77.6–79.8%); ~10,900 useful prefetch loads vs ~2,450 wasted / ~790 late per run (81% precision). Disk timer −5 to −7.7 s/run.
measurements.source: internal findings, not staged #31, #32

measurements.display: (b) Throughput as a shipped default, same matrix: godot_controller −7.64%, rust_queue −0.70%, typescript_websocket −6.96% paired tok/s → median −6.96%. Mechanism: attention +4.8–6.3 s (unified-memory bandwidth contention) and a new 1.3–2.3 s layer-barrier wait outweigh the disk savings; ~13,700 prefetch-driven cache evictions per run.
measurements.source: internal findings, not staged #49; internal findings, not staged

entries.notes: The prediction is real and essentially harvests the full Belady gap (internal findings, not staged #32: 14.2-point LRU-vs-Belady gap at pin=0); the cost of acting on it (loads + barrier + cache churn) exceeds what it saves. This exact split — 'the prediction is real, the speed claim isn't' — is why PILOT stays opt-in, never a throughput default (README.md 'Settled verdicts'). Two harness bugs had to be fixed before this number could be trusted: a brace-group exit that silently ended the whole matrix after one warmup (internal findings, not staged #23), and unfrozen .fa_usage state that made hash gates unpassable by construction (internal findings, not staged #48, fixed in commit 3f6327d). REGIME CAUTION (per external review, this is the case the Regime field exists for): the S>4 prefill-regime acceleration (Metal prefill kernel, and the modeled DSA-metal design study) does NOT revive this verdict. PILOT K6's loss mechanism is S=1 decode-time unified-memory bandwidth contention between speculative prefetch loads and the attention path — a DECODE-regime cost that prefill-side acceleration does not touch at all. Reconsideration requires a DECODE regime change: DSA-aware decode (design-study §5.5 scope, not yet gated), mixed precision, or a materially different cache residency — not a prefill-regime one. The earlier 'revival owed once DSA + Metal prefill change the attention-cost side of the ledger' framing (internal findings, not staged #27) is corrected by this narrower regime analysis: prefill and decode are different regimes and a win in one says nothing about the other.

entries.name: Prefetch-aware eviction veto + adaptive-K ("PILOT salvage")

regime.context: ps-matrix-20260714, 3 held-out prompts × 3 rotated trials
regime.cache: 34–52 LRU slots/layer, frozen profile
regime.backend: CPU

entries.hypothesis: After PILOT K6's throughput revert, keep PILOT's accurate predictions but stop paying for speculative loads — steer LRU eviction away from router-predicted experts (no loads, no barrier) and adapt K from router-score entropy — a cheaper way to spend the same intelligence.
entries.prediction: None recorded numerically; framed as a 'free win' candidate because it reuses an already-validated predictor.

measurements.display: Paired throughput −26.32%, −35.22%, −20.89% → median −26.32%; expert hit rate +0.0 points on all three prompts; disk time +6 to +17 s worse. Flags-off byte-identical (implementation verified correct — the idea failed, not the code).
measurements.source: internal findings, not staged #50

measurements.display: New-math variable-size cache oracle (heterogeneous int4 18.9153MB / repaired-int2 10.027MB manifest mix vs. uniform int4, byte-LRU vs. offline demand-Belady and bypass-Belady, RAM-matched per-layer budget, pins frozen): whole-trace offline gap (B_LRU-B_oracle)/B_LRU = 31.6-33.6% across baseline/coding/shotgun and both the manifest and uniform-int4 layouts (demand-Belady alone 31.6-33.3%; admission-bypass Belady adds only about +0.3 points more; the heterogeneous manifest mix sits close to the uniform-size result, not systematically different). In request terms, uniform-int4 @ 48.88GB pins: live hit 69.75% vs. offline demand-Belady 79.79% = 10.04 hit points -- this REPRODUCES the already-committed route-study cache-sim at PIN=48GB to within noise (overnight-20260714-001239/cache-sim-baseline.txt: 69.79% vs 79.79%, 9.99-point gap; the small residual is usage-file drift, 2537 vs 2584 pins). The large offline gap is NOT new information and NOT a heterogeneity effect -- it is the SAME LRU-vs-Belady gap this entry's own verdict already priced, now confirmed to persist unchanged when expert sizes are heterogeneous.
measurements.source: the new-math replay results Task 2b; oracle-summary.json, oracle-policies.csv; cross-ref overnight-20260714-001239/cache-sim-baseline.txt (commit 0af7371)

measurements.display: Three online eviction policies tested against byte-LRU at the same heterogeneous-size budgets: GreedyDual-Size with cost=size is PROVABLY and empirically identical to byte-LRU (verified byte-exact on every trace/layout row, zero warnings -- when miss cost is proportional to size the GDS value density collapses to a constant, i.e. GDS(cost=size) degenerates algebraically to LRU); SNRD (evict max size x staleness) and GDS cost=1 (pure miss-count objective) equal byte-LRU under uniform sizes and are 0.1-0.5% WORSE under the heterogeneous manifest mix. PRECISE SCOPE (per external review): none of the TESTED online heterogeneous-size-aware policies beat byte-LRU on the available traces -- sufficient to keep online cache-policy work unfunded, but not a claim that no possible online policy ever could.
measurements.source: the new-math replay results Task 2b policy table (commit 0af7371)

measurements.display: Per the study's own kill-line wording (gap < 2% => frontier stays closed; measured 31.6-33.6% exceeds it), the closed-frontier verdict is now explicitly regime-scoped: CLOSED for the ONLINE eviction policies actually tested (none of them beat byte-LRU on the available traces, heterogeneous expert sizes included -- confirming this entry's own uniform-size veto result survives the heterogeneous regime), OPEN only in OFFLINE/future-knowledge terms (a genuinely predictive router-lookahead could in principle harvest the ~10-hit-point gap -- but pilot-k6-router-lookahead-prefetch already tried exactly that lookahead mechanism and found the prediction real while its cost, loads plus barrier plus cache churn, ate the win). Admission control (the one mechanism class not previously tested here) adds only about 0.3 points on top of pure replacement -- no hidden admission-control prize either.
measurements.source: the new-math replay results Task 2b verdict and interpretation (commit 0af7371)

entries.notes:
At 34–52 LRU slots/layer with ~8 random experts touched per layer per token, reuse distance is longer than any realistic cache — which victim you evict barely matters. This result, combined with PILOT K6's revert and persistent Metal state's null result, is what the project calls 'the cache-policy frontier closed': capacity vs. reuse distance is the wall, not the replacement policy.

REGIME-ROBUSTNESS CONFIRMATION (2026-07-15, commit 0af7371, new-math offline study, c/tools/variable_size_cache_oracle.py): re-ran the demand-Belady/admission-bypass/SNRD/GDS comparison under HETEROGENEOUS expert sizes (int4 18.9153MB + repaired-int2 10.027MB manifest mix, not just the uniform sizes this entry's own veto A/B used) and found the same closed-for-online-policies verdict holds unchanged: GDS(cost=size) is algebraically and empirically byte-LRU; SNRD and GDS(cost=1) are equal-or-worse under heterogeneous sizes. PRECISION NOTE (per external review): this is stated as 'none of the tested online heterogeneous-size policies beat byte-LRU on the available traces,' not as a proof that no online policy ever could -- the scoped claim is sufficient to keep online cache-policy work unfunded without overclaiming impossibility. The large offline (LRU-vs-Belady) gap this exposes (31.6-33.6%) is not new information and not a heterogeneity artifact -- it decomposes to the exact same ~10-hit-point gap the committed route-study cache-sim already showed at PIN=48GB (69.79->79.79%), the same gap PILOT K6's real lookahead prediction already harvested and then lost to its own overhead (pilot-k6-router-lookahead-prefetch), and the same gap this entry's own veto experiment already showed a passive eviction-side intervention cannot monetize. Status unchanged (mechanism/performance Falsified, shipping Dead) -- this is confirmation that the (precisely-scoped) verdict generalizes to heterogeneous sizes, not a new result reopening the frontier.

entries.name: Heterogeneous CPU/GPU MoE tail

regime.context: 112 tokens, 3 trials/mode
regime.cache: ~66% hit rate (measured regime)
regime.backend: CPU+Metal hybrid (ragged grouped CPU MoE, PR #3)

entries.hypothesis: Running small missed-expert tails on the CPU concurrently with Metal executing resident experts hides miss latency behind compute.
entries.prediction: None recorded numerically; the design (ragged grouped CPU MoE, PR #3, unit-tested exact) was expected to be a net win by overlapping I/O-bound misses with GPU compute.

measurements.display: Metal-only 1.43 tok/s (baseline); forced heterogeneous (CPU handles all misses) 1.25 tok/s (−12.6%); automatic CPU tail (small miss tails only) 1.34 tok/s (−6.3%). Attention GPU-wall time grew 19.7s→27.3s under hetero — CPU kernels stole unified-memory bandwidth from Metal's attention path; disk I/O was unchanged (~38–40s in every mode).
measurements.source: internal findings, not staged #45; internal findings, not staged

entries.notes: Regime-dependent, not categorically dead — at the measured 66% hit rate, CPU compute for misses competes with Metal for bandwidth; at a hypothetical ~95% hit rate (0.4 misses/token) the same design could hide in Metal's shadow. The gating variable is hit rate, not the kernel.

entries.name: Serve-mode prefix KV reuse + delta-only prefill

regime.cache: .ili_kv persistent KV slots
regime.backend: CPU/Metal (serve loop)

entries.hypothesis: A long-lived ili serve process with monotonic conversation history and persistent KV slots can match each turn's prompt against a stored prefix and prefill only the new delta, instead of re-prefilling the whole history every turn.
entries.prediction: Roadmap Step 1 target: ~114 min/20-turn session, TTFT 5–15 s (docs/roadmap-daily-driver.md).

measurements.display: Delta-only prefill exact per the engine's own [API] counters — turn 2 matched prefix 1639/3096 tokens, prefilled only 1457; turn 3 matched 3395/4932, prefilled 1537 — never a full re-prefill.
measurements.source: c/scripts/serve_gate.py run 'serve-gate-20260714'

measurements.display: An initial N=1 observation (.ili_kv persistence across a server restart: slot 0 resumed 3,249 tokens in 0.1 s; the next request prefilled 0 tokens — TTFT 3.07 s vs 436.65 s cold, 142x) was retired as uncitable: the cold and resume observations used different prompts, and neither stated whether TTFT included process/model load. Certified replacement (2026-07-20): a same-prompt, randomized ABBA/BAAB cold-vs-resume harness, n=6 trials/arm — cold median TTFT 153.92s [145.99, 163.49], resume median TTFT 22.56s [19.18, 30.97], speedup 6.8x [5.0x, 8.0x] (percentile bootstrap). Decode unchanged with reuse: 1.56–1.66 tok/s vs 1.45 tok/s on a nonce-broken fresh-context control (settled warm band 1.42–1.58).

entries.notes: The rare feature that verified exactly as designed on the first gated run, because the gate checked the engine's own counters, not just end-to-end timings. The new wall it exposed: measured serve prefill throughput is only ~1.0–1.8 tok/s (the roadmap had assumed 100–200 tok/s, wrong by ~100x), so TTFT ≤15 s holds only for deltas ≲ 25 tokens — which is what the next several entries address.

entries.name: "Serve prefill is disk-bound" — I/O-bandwidth fix (falsified before implementation)

regime.context: 1361-token turn (gate 0); 821–1884s measured TTFTs
regime.cache: n/a (diagnostic)
regime.backend: CPU (pre-Metal-prefill-kernel)

entries.hypothesis: Batch prefill streams nearly all 256 experts (~4.9 GB) per MoE layer per >1K-token turn, so serve-mode prefill is disk-bound at roughly decode speed; raising effective read bandwidth (the serve-gate's implied ~0.15–0.35 GB/s) toward ~5 GB/s via layout-aware ordering, bigger reads, or deeper queues would fix TTFT.
entries.prediction: An I/O-only fix targeting ~5 GB/s effective bandwidth was the original plan; the prefill-I/O study §4 predicts this fix 'would change TTFT by roughly nothing' once tested against the real bottleneck.

measurements.display: The raw SSD already sustains 13.3–13.5 GB/s at the engine's exact read pattern (19 MB blocks, F_NOCACHE, 8 threads; 390 GB full-shard sweep, 3x RAM, page-cache-proof) — ~2x the 5–7 GB/s the plan assumed as its target, and needing no layout/read-size/queue-depth fix. Pure-disk floor per turn = 284.5 GB / 13.3 GB/s ≈ 21.4 s, against measured TTFTs of 821–1884 s: a 38–88x gap between implied (0.15–0.35 GB/s) and raw (13.3 GB/s) bandwidth.
measurements.source: the prefill-I/O study §§1–2, 7; internal findings, not staged #54

measurements.display: TTFT/(prefill tokens × total context) is nearly constant (182/201/216 µs/token-pair) across turns with different disk-byte volumes — the signature of quadratic CPU attention, confirmed in-engine by gate 0 (commit 8d26555): a 1361-token turn measured attention 84.8% of TTFT, expert-disk 0.7%.
measurements.source: the prefill-I/O study §§1–2, 7; commit 8d26555

entries.hypothesis: Chunking prefill into bounded-size steps (O(chunk) transient memory instead of O(prompt)) lets very large one-shot prompts complete without the memory/swap pressure a monolithic forward pass creates.
entries.prediction: None numerically recorded ahead of the fix; the implicit target was 'byte-identical output, large prompts no longer freeze.'

measurements.display: Greedy output byte-identical vs. the monolithic path on the standard prompts; a 1.5 MB synthetic GLM-shaped fixture drives the real serve loop through >128 KB payloads, chunked==monolithic equivalence confirmed; 105 python+C tests green under make test METAL=1.

entries.notes: SPLIT per external review: the semantic-equivalence claim (chunked forward produces byte-identical output vs. monolithic) is Confirmed on a synthetic fixture plus the standard prompt set — that is a mechanism/correctness claim, not a survival claim. Real-744B, real-40K-prompt survival and the peak-memory reduction it's supposed to buy are unmeasured and Provisional: the original triggering incident (a real 40K-token monolithic prefill pushing ~8GB of transients into swap under a synchronous GPU wait) motivated this fix, but no committed record yet re-runs that same real long prompt with chunking enabled end-to-end. Progress-heartbeat instrumentation shipped alongside the fix specifically to make that confirmation observable (chunked prefill logs progress rather than going silent for tens of minutes); it will confirm survival + peak-memory reduction on the next real long run. This fix replaced an earlier, now-falsified diagnosis — a suspected 64 KB pipe write-deadlock between openai_server.py and the engine — which a tiny-fixture sweep (1 KB–256 KB payloads) showed never occurs at any size; disassembly instead found the process was tens of minutes into a single monolithic S=39,749 step() call whose ~8 GB of transients had pushed it into swap, compounded by a synchronous GPU wait under ILI_METAL_PREFILL=1 (internal findings, not staged #29 and internal findings, not staged #55 for the full corrected account — a rare case of the project's own mid-investigation diagnosis being wrong and caught by the same adversarial-verification standard applied to agent output). A separate, unrelated scaffold-gate bug in long_ctx_profile.py's engine-ownership check (it refused to run whenever any glm process existed, blocking its own documented start-serve-then-profile workflow) was fixed the same campaign in commit 62c2c65 — a tooling fix, not a performance change (internal findings, not staged #30).

measurements.display: GATE A CROSS-CHECK (2026-07-15, tiered-int4-int2-mixed-precision-container's defective-quantizer 280GB build): the container built by greedily demoting experts using this entry's own flat error ranking collapsed outright on a 3-prompt long-generation test (independently verified degenerate repetition loops -- e.g. prompt 2 looping "the C source-compiler's," ad infinitum; c/bench-m5max/container-20260715/collapse-p2.txt, gates.log). This is a TWO-PART refinement, not a reversal. Part 1: ranking usefulness FALSIFIED (flat across experts) -- the pre-existing flat 0.88-0.92 per-expert measurement is the actual evidentiary basis for this, and gate A's real-world collapse is read as practical corroboration (a container built on this flat ranking's demotion order failed) rather than independent proof of flatness. A real threshold requires calibrating this instrument's absolute-error reading across a SEPARATION of known-good and known-bad points -- the int4 reference, this defective int2, at least one repaired int2, and ideally an intermediate variant -- with the threshold read off where quality actually breaks across that separation, not off one dead build.
measurements.source: c/bench-m5max/container-20260715/{collapse-summary.csv,gates.log,collapse-p1.txt,collapse-p2.txt} (2026-07-15 gate A run); independent verification; campaign-log.md 17:19:17, 17:23:12, 17:30:33, 17:37:02 entries

mechanism.display: Current int2 reconstruction-error ranking invalidated by a defective/high-floor quantizer (qmax=1 ternary behavior, -2 code unused, ~89% of Gaussian weights zeroed; floor 0.868 vs 0.343 optimal). Expert discriminability remains unknown pending a repaired quantizer and a ranking-reliability test. GATE A UPDATE (2026-07-15): ranking usefulness is now treated as FALSIFIED outright for this quantizer, not merely unknown-pending-repair -- a real container built on this ranking's greedy demotion order collapsed (see gate-A cross-check measurement above). Whether a REPAIRED quantizer's ranking would discriminate real experts is still untested and remains open.

performance.display: Unknown — no discriminating signal has been recovered from a validated instrument; the flat 0.88–0.92 spread is confounded with the quantizer's own saturation and must not be read as evidence of uniform expert damageability (invalidated-without-validation, not proven-uninformative). GATE A UPDATE (2026-07-15): split verdict -- the RANKING use of this signal is falsified (see mechanism); the ABSOLUTE-MAGNITUDE use is a candidate reject-side warning only (gate A's collapse is consistent with high uniform error predicting global failure), not a validated kill-threshold -- see notes/measurement for the cross-quantizer calibration this would need before it is one.

entries.notes:
Root cause (external review, code-verified): tools/convert_fp8_to_int4.py's quant_int2 sets qmax=(1<<(bits-1))-1=1 for bits=2, so scale=absmax/qmax=absmax/1 and codes=clip(rint(w/s),-2,1) — the -2 code is geometrically unreachable (verified histogram on 64x1024 Gaussian: {-1:2846, 0:59816, +1:2874}, zero occurrences of -2) and ~89% of a Gaussian row's weights round to zero. It is a ternary quantizer wearing 2-bit clothing, not a genuine 4-level one — hence the 0.868 rel-Frobenius floor against the true 4-level Lloyd-Max optimum of 0.3428 (int4, by contrast, is healthy: 0.143 vs the 16-level optimum's 0.0975, ~1.47x). Committed evidence: c/tests/test_quant_noise_floor.py now (1) pins the code-utilization defect directly as a regression trip-wire (asserts code -2 occurs zero times on synthetic Gaussian, to be updated/inverted when the quantizer is repaired) and (2) carries a reference repaired quantizer as the seed of the real fix, not the fix itself.

The repair path has three separate stages, deliberately not conflated into one number: (1) Format-compatible fitted-scale repair — keep the shipped {-2,-1,0,1} codebook and dequant ((code-2)*scale, zero engine change), replace the shipped absmax/1 scale with a per-row scale chosen by grid search minimizing reconstruction MSE. The committed test's reference implementation of exactly this measures 0.380 relative Frobenius on synthetic Gaussian weights (evidence_class synthetic-fixture, c/tests/test_quant_noise_floor.py) — a weight-Frobenius proxy on the easiest possible distribution, NOT a model-quality claim. A ~0.45-0.55 floor on real expert weights is an ESTIMATE, unmeasured pending implementation against actual model tensors — real weight rows are not i.i.d. Gaussian and may fare worse than this synthetic best case. (2) Best 2-bit design — a symmetric codebook (e.g. {-3,-1,1,3} in place of {-2,-1,0,1}) is a true mid-rise 2-bit quantizer with no wasted zero level; same 2-bit storage, but changed dequant semantics that the current engine does not implement (neither the CPU AVX2/NEON int2 matmul nor the Metal fmt==3 kernel decode this formula) — requires a kernel touch, not just a tooling-side fix. (3) Task-sensitive evaluation — every number above, measured or estimated, is weight-Frobenius error, a cheap proxy. The real test is activation-output error (||W4x - W2x|| / ||W4x|| on representative activations x, not the weight matrices in isolation) and, beyond that, actual downstream benchmark quality — weight Frobenius alone, in either direction, is never sufficient evidence of real model-quality impact.

Reviewer's caveat, preserved in substance: a biased, compressed ruler can still retain SOME ranking information even while its absolute error floor is high — this entry's mechanism finding is that the per-expert ranking is invalidated-without-validation, not proven-uninformative. The flat 0.88–0.92 spread could be hiding real per-expert structure this instrument is too coarse to resolve, or could be genuinely flat; only a repaired quantizer plus a dedicated ranking-reliability test (e.g. confirming known-different experts resolve apart once the floor drops) can tell the two apart.

GATE A REFINEMENT (2026-07-15, two-part, not a reversal): (1) ranking usefulness FALSIFIED -- the flat 0.88-0.92 per-expert spread is now treated as genuinely flat, not merely instrument-saturated-but-possibly-hiding-structure; a real container built on this ranking's demotion order collapsed under gate A (tiered-int4-int2-mixed-precision-container). (2) absolute magnitude is a REJECT-SIDE WARNING / candidate fail-fast predictor, not a confirmed kill-threshold: gate A's collapse is CONSISTENT WITH high uniform error (~0.868) predicting global failure, but one dead build does not establish a universal numeric threshold -- that needs calibration across a SEPARATION of points (int4 reference, this defective int2, >=1 repaired int2, ideally an intermediate variant), with the threshold read from where quality actually breaks across that separation. See container-quantizer-validation-sequence for how this feeds the required pre-build activation-level gate.

EXTERNAL-PANEL REVIEW UPDATE (2026-07-15, revised round 2): this entry's own prediction cites 'the roadmap's ~2.0-2.2 tok/s projection' (the offline math-verdict record Study 4; docs/roadmap-daily-driver.md 'Bottom line') as the ceiling this technique was originally scoped to help reach. That figure predates the compute-floor work this file's m1-c2 entries (2026-07-15 external-panel proposal batch) now scope -- it assumed hit-rate/routing levers only, with the ~0.36-0.38 s/token non-disk floor treated as fixed. RECORDED HERE AS A SCENARIO TABLE, not a single replacement figure (round 2 supersedes an earlier single-point '3.0-3.5 tok/s' framing): CENTRAL 2.3-2.8 tok/s (h=0.78, BW_exposed=10 GB/s, compute floor C=0.27 s/token, thermal derate theta_thermal=1.08x) is the realistic expectation; AGGRESSIVE 3.0-3.5 tok/s requires nearly every favorable assumption in this batch to hold simultaneously (m1's upper hit-rate, a1's lower compute floor, p2's best-case exposed bandwidth, a2/p3/m3's overlap, minimal thermal derate); >3.5 tok/s is considered unlikely without an outright kernel breakthrough (p2 finding M5's tensor path genuinely delivers the 1.5-3x upside rather than the 0-10% wrapper-only case). DSA holds >1 tok/s at long context per dsa-metal-kernel-design-study's crossover tables and a3's decode extension, replacing the old ceiling's silence on long context entirely.

Full model (t_token in s/token; tok/s = 1/t_token):

  t_token = theta_thermal * [ C + 600*(1-H)*b_e/BW_exposed - O_overlap ]

where: theta_thermal = thermal/power derating multiplier (>=1; 1.0 = no derate; measured by p2's power-constrained STEADY-STATE roofline, NOT its cold first-5-min roofline); C = non-disk compute floor, s/token (today ~0.36, a1's target 0.25-0.29); 600 = routed-expert-layer instances per token (8 experts/layer x 75 main MoE layers, the offline math-verdict record); H = expert-cache hit rate (today ~0.65, m1's modeled 0.80-0.83); b_e = bytes per missed expert load, heterogeneous by tier (18.9153 MB int4, 9.458 MB today's defective int2, ~10.1-10.7 MB m1's repaired int2); BW_exposed = the EXPOSED critical-path bandwidth from p2's probe (compulsory miss bytes / main-thread storage stall -- NOT device throughput, NOT read-path throughput; see p2-m5-gpu-tensor-path-probe notes for the three-way distinction); O_overlap = per-token time hidden via compute/IO overlap (a2, p3, m3's mechanisms), s/token, subtracted directly.

CONSISTENCY CHECK: at today's baseline (H=0.65, b_e=18.9153 MB, BW_exposed taken as device throughput 13.3 GB/s absent any overlap mechanism today, O_overlap=0, theta_thermal=1.0), the formula gives 600*0.35*18.9153 MB / 13.3 GB/s = 0.298 s, matching this file's already-settled ~0.30 s/token miss term (docs/roadmap-daily-driver.md, README.md) almost exactly -- the formula reproduces the existing settled figure before any of this batch's proposed changes are applied, which is the load-bearing sanity check for trusting it going forward. TOOLING NOTE: the core C + B_miss/BW relationship inside this formula is not just a paper model -- c/tools/simulate_bytes_cache.py (committed 2026-07-15, commit 16bbffc) already implements it directly as a --bw-gbs sensitivity sweep (t = c_seconds + steady_bytes_per_tok/BW) over multiple container layouts, with B_miss bytes/token computed as its documented authoritative output; it does not yet include this formula's theta_thermal or O_overlap terms, which remain this batch's own extensions (theta_thermal from p2's steady-state roofline, O_overlap from a2/p3/m3) on top of that tool's core sensitivity model. This entry's own technique and gate are unaffected by any of the above (Ke bracketing, quality-gate requirement); only the roadmap-level ceiling it was originally framed against has moved, and moved because of compute- and disk-side work (a1, m1-m3, p2) this entry's own offline simulation did not model.

entries.name: KV-slot allocation economics

regime.context: 3 traces, calibrated within ~1 point of measured hit rate
regime.backend: n/a (config/provisioning guidance)

entries.hypothesis: Provisioning more KV-cache slots (for concurrent agent sessions) has a calculable cost in evicted expert-cache capacity that can be weighed against the prefill time it saves when a slot maps to a real live session.
entries.prediction: None recorded numerically ahead of the study; the roadmap had only a general warning ('4 slots would steal ~29 GB from the expert cache').

measurements.display: hit-rate fit hit(GB) ≈ 64.7 + 25.4·ln(GB/97.1); each KV slot costs ~1.9–2.3 hit points = 1.3–3.6 min/session of slower decode; a slot mapped to a live session saves ~32–35 min/session; benefit:cost ~10–25x when used, pure loss when idle. Two sessions sharing one slot is the worst configuration (mutual KV eviction — near-full re-prefill every turn). Robust across both disk-fit models and all three traces.
measurements.source: the offline math-verdict record Study 5

entries.notes:
STALENESS FLAG per external review: the closed-form economic model itself (the hit(GB) fit, and the general cost-of-lost-hit-points arithmetic) remains confirmed. But the specific 32–35 min/session and 10–25x benefit:cost figures predate the Metal prefill kernel — a slot's 'benefit' side of the ratio is the prefill time a live session saves by not re-prefilling, and the Metal prefill kernel makes context rebuilds roughly 4–8x cheaper (a conservative haircut of the 6.3–9.1x wall-clock TTFT measurement in the Metal prefill attention kernel entry, applied to the narrower 'cost of a context rebuild' framing rather than full end-to-end TTFT) than when this study's benefit-side numbers were computed. The cost side (hit points lost per GB stolen from the expert cache) is unaffected by the prefill kernel and still holds as measured. Net effect: benefit:cost is smaller than 10–25x now, direction of the remaining margin unknown without rerunning Study 5's benefit-side arithmetic against post-kernel prefill costs — current operational ratio is Provisional pending recalculation. Shipped guidance is unchanged qualitatively (set --kv-slots = number of concurrent sessions, exactly; never provision idle slots) since the cost-of-idle-slot conclusion doesn't depend on the stale benefit figure, but the magnitude claim does.

EXTERNAL-PANEL REVIEW UPDATE (2026-07-15, revised round 2): the panel's revised decode-throughput picture is a SCENARIO TABLE, not a single figure -- see topp-adaptive-expert-routing's notes for the full t_token model, variable definitions, and the consistency check tying it back to this file's already-settled ~0.30 s/token miss term. CENTRAL 2.3-2.8 tok/s (h=0.78, BW_exposed=10 GB/s, compute floor 0.27 s/token, thermal derate 1.08x); AGGRESSIVE 3.0-3.5 tok/s (needs nearly every favorable assumption in the m1-c2 batch simultaneously); >3.5 tok/s unlikely without an outright kernel breakthrough (p2's tensor-path probe finding real upside rather than the wrapper-only case). This touches the session-economics picture here because a slot's total session-minutes cost/benefit bakes in an assumed decode rate alongside the prefill-rebuild cost this entry's own STALENESS FLAG already addresses. Recorded here as a placeholder needing its own recalculation, not yet performed: this entry's 1.3-3.6 min/session cost and 32-35 min/session benefit figures assumed the OLD ~2.0-2.2 tok/s roadmap ceiling throughout; even the CENTRAL 2.3-2.8 tok/s scenario above would shrink the decode-time component of a session's total minutes further, on top of the prefill-side shrinkage the STALENESS FLAG already flags. Operational guidance (set --kv-slots = number of concurrent sessions, exactly) is unaffected either way; the magnitude of the benefit:cost ratio has now drifted on BOTH its prefill-rebuild-cost axis (STALENESS FLAG, already recorded) and its decode-rate axis (this update) since Study 5 was computed, and both need a joint recalculation against the CENTRAL scenario specifically (not the AGGRESSIVE one), not two independent patches.

entries.name: Groupwise symmetric int2 tier (fitted-scale codebook, group-64/128 scales)

regime.context: external-panel proposal, 2026-07-15, not yet built; extends stage 2 of expert-quant-error-saliency's 3-stage repair plan with concrete group-granularity sizing
regime.cache: expert cache; modeled hit rate 0.65 -> 0.80-0.83 from higher resident capacity at smaller expert size (hypothesis; see falsifier)
regime.container: proposed: symmetric {-3,-1,1,3} fitted-scale codebook, group-64/group-128 scales, ~10.1-10.7 MB/expert (53-56% of int4's 18.9153 MB; today's shipped defective per-row-scale int2 is 9.458 MB)
regime.backend: CPU/Metal (int2 kernels exist per-row-scale only; group-scale decode is a new matmul_i2/fmt==3 variant, not yet implemented)

entries.hypothesis: expert-quant-error-saliency's own notes name a 3-stage repair plan: (1) format-compatible fitted-scale repair, measured 0.380 relative Frobenius on synthetic Gaussian weights -- close to the true 4-level Lloyd-Max optimum of 0.3428 (the Shannon vector-quantization bound at this rate is ~0.25), i.e. the fitted-scale result is already near scalar-optimal and further scalar tuning has little left to give; (2) a true symmetric mid-rise codebook ({-3,-1,1,3}, no wasted zero level), which needs a kernel touch; (3) task-sensitive evaluation via activation-output error, not weight Frobenius alone. This entry is stage (2) made concrete -- group-64/128 fitted scales (finer than today's per-row scale) on the symmetric codebook, sized and hit-rate-modeled, with stage (3)'s activation-output-error test as a later falsifier. The panel's point in naming it explicitly: further gains have to come from groupwise/variable-rate granularity (this entry, and m2), not more scalar-scale tuning.
entries.prediction: Sizing: ~10.1-10.7 MB/expert (53-56% of int4's 18.9153 MB) for the repaired groupwise tier, above today's defective 9.458 MB per-row-scale int2 because finer group scales cost more overhead bytes for a much lower error floor. Original panel prediction: modeled effective hit rate 0.65 -> 0.80-0.83 -> decode 2.0-2.3 tok/s (1.35-1.55x), i.e. a +21%..+49% delta bracket. MEASURED (2026-07-15, commit 16bbffc, c/tools/simulate_bytes_cache.py against the three existing route traces): steady-state B_miss bytes/token -- A (uniform int4, today) 2.89-3.06 GB/tok; B (existing shipped 280 GB defective manifest) 1.71-1.82; C (stage-1 fitted-scale repair, per-row scale, ENGINE-READY today, zero kernel change, at current slot-count LRU) 1.52-1.62; D (same stage-1 repair at RAM-matched byte-budget LRU, an engine change) 1.29-1.38; this entry's OWN groupwise tier (stage 2, needs a new kernel), byte-budget mode: E-g128f16 1.37 GB/tok, E-g128f32 1.47 GB/tok. At the empirically anchored ~10 GB/s exposed bandwidth (measured disk timers imply ~9.5-10.5 GB/s effective, not assumed): C = 1.92-1.95 tok/s (+26.5-27.6% vs A), D = 2.01-2.04 tok/s (+32.6-33.7%), this entry's own E-g128f16/f32 (byte mode) = +30.5-31.4% / +28.0-28.9% -- ALL decisively nearer the original +21% floor than the +49% ceiling. The +49%-class scenario is REFUTED at measured bandwidth: it would require ~5 GB/s effective disk bandwidth, which the measured timers contradict. Measured decode hit rate on layout A (today, this replay's own traces): h=0.731-0.741 -- higher than the ~0.65 figure this file uses elsewhere (c1's hypothesis, kv-slot-allocation-economics); both are measured, on different trace/config combinations (this replay's 128-token traces vs the K6-matrix's live engine capture), and the discrepancy is flagged rather than silently resolved, per this file's standing convention for cross-source disagreements (see source_conflicts).

measurements.display: Modeled 10.1-10.7 MB/expert = 53-56% of int4's 18.9153 MB (the container-design plan); vs today's shipped defective per-row-scale int2 at 9.458 MB (the offline math-verdict record Study 1) -- the extra ~0.6-1.2 MB/expert buys finer (group-64/128, not per-row) scale granularity on a true symmetric {-3,-1,1,3} codebook.
measurements.source: external-panel proposal, 2026-07-15; sizing baseline the container-design plan, the offline math-verdict record Study 1

measurements.display: FIRST FALSIFIER (offline, zero engine time, run before any activation-error work), REVISED PER EXTERNAL REVIEW (round 2): evaluate explicit container layouts side by side through a BYTE-CAPACITY-AWARE simulator -- heterogeneous expert sizes per layout (not one scalar expert-size for a whole run), byte-exact eviction (evict by bytes, not by expert count), pinned bytes + LRU bytes + page-cache bytes as THREE SEPARATE capacity pools. This tooling ALREADY EXISTS (c/tools/simulate_bytes_cache.py, committed 2026-07-15 as commit 16bbffc, extends simulate_m5max_cache.py exactly this way) with the layouts this falsifier needs built in: A = uniform int4 (18.9153 MB, no tiering); B = the existing shipped mixed manifest (the container-design plan's 280 GB defective-int2 build); C/D = a per-row fitted-scale repaired tier (stage 1 of the repair plan) at slot-count vs byte-budget LRU respectively -- D is where allocate_bit_budget.py's own open design question #1 (the container-design plan, 'engine cache accounting is slot-count-based... the capacity half of the predicted gain only materializes if... accounting goes per-byte') gets directly operationalized; E-* = groupwise-scale sensitivity variants (group-128, f16 or f32 scale bytes) at both slot-count and byte-budget LRU -- this entry's own m1 proposal specifically. Required output: B_miss bytes/token per layout (the tool's own documented 'authoritative output'; its --bw-gbs tok/s column is sensitivity-only), against the existing route traces (routes-baseline.bin, routes-coding.bin, routes-shotgun.bin) -- not a hit-rate percentage, which would conflate misses of different byte sizes across layouts.
measurements.source: external-panel proposal, 2026-07-15; falsifier tooling c/tools/simulate_bytes_cache.py (committed, commit 16bbffc), docs/m5max-route-trace-cache-sim.md, the container-design plan

measurements.display: SECOND falsifier (after the three-layout byte-capacity replay clears, before any full build): activation-output error ||W4x - W2x|| / ||W4x|| on 128 sampled experts stratified across early/mid/late layers (not weight-Frobenius alone -- expert-quant-error-saliency's own notes name this the real test), plus a router-weighted layer-output error and a final-logit KL divergence; reject any codebook not materially below the defective quantizer's error on this metric. A layer-stratified mini-container (a handful of experts per stratum, not the full 19,200) proves the format before any full build.
measurements.source: external-panel proposal, 2026-07-15; methodology named in performance-theory.json expert-quant-error-saliency notes

measurements.display: Full A/B/C/D/E-* layout grid (steady-state B_miss bytes/token, the replay's own documented authoritative output; tok/s columns are sensitivity-only, t=C+B_miss/BW with C=0.36 s held fixed): A 2.89-3.06 GB/tok (baseline); B 1.71-1.82 (0.59-0.60x A); C 1.52-1.62 (0.53x A); D 1.29-1.38 (0.45x A); E-g128f16-byte 1.374 (this entry's own groupwise sizing); E-g128f32-byte 1.474. Pin-source sensitivity (rerun against the .fa_usage.coding histogram instead of the primary frozen .fa_usage): same ordering, same ratios within 3 percentage points -- the adjudication is robust to which frozen histogram ranks the pins. Byte-budget cache accounting is worth roughly +6 percentage points of throughput ON TOP OF the repaired container alone (D's +32.6-33.7% vs C's +26.5-27.6% at BW=10, holding the quantizer repair fixed) -- this is an ENGINE change (cap_for_ram/ecap accounting moving from slot-count to per-byte, the container-design plan's own open design question #1), separable from and additive to the quantizer repair itself.
measurements.source: the offline-replay results (commit 16bbffc, produced by c/tools/simulate_bytes_cache.py against routes-baseline.bin, routes-coding.bin, routes-shotgun.bin; validated within 0.4pp of the offline math-verdict record Study 1's own anchors)

entries.notes:
CHEAP FALSIFIER, run in this order, cheapest first: (1) OFFLINE, ZERO ENGINE TIME -- run c/tools/simulate_bytes_cache.py's layouts A (uniform int4), B (existing manifest), C/D (per-row repaired tier, slot vs byte-budget LRU), and E-* (groupwise tier, this entry's own proposal) side by side with --miss-structure, reporting B_miss bytes/token per layout against the existing committed route traces -- the tool already exists (committed 2026-07-15, commit 16bbffc) and implements the heterogeneous-size, byte-exact-eviction, three-pool (pin/LRU/page-cache) accounting this falsifier needs; this is a RUN, not a BUILD. REVISED PER EXTERNAL REVIEW (round 2): this replaces an earlier framing of this entry that treated the existing container's +21% (the offline math-verdict record Study 1) and this entry's own +49%-ceiling hypothesis as a single bracket needing reconciliation -- they are different experiments on different containers, and the A/B/C/D/E layout comparison is what actually answers whether the repaired tier beats the existing manifest, not a floor/ceiling framing of two incommensurate numbers. (2) Only if (1) clears: activation-output error on 128 stratified sampled experts + router-weighted layer-output error + final-logit KL, reject codebooks not materially below the defective quantizer. (3) Only if (2) clears: a layer-stratified mini-container before any full 19,200-expert build. This extends the existing 3-stage repair plan's stage 2 (performance-theory.json, expert-quant-error-saliency) with concrete sizing; the panel separately notes the stage-1 fitted-scale result (0.380 relative Frobenius) is already near scalar-optimal (Lloyd-Max 4-level optimum 0.3428; Shannon vector-quantization bound at this rate ~0.25), so further gains have to come from groupwise/variable-rate granularity (this entry, and m2), not more scalar-scale tuning. Cost estimate: falsifier (1) is CPU-only, reuses existing traces and existing tooling -- the simulator-engineering work this falsifier would otherwise have needed (heterogeneous sizing, byte-exact eviction, three-pool capacity accounting) is already done; what remains is choosing a manifest/usage input and running it, on the order of minutes to an hour, no engine time. Falsifier (2) is a few hours of dequant/requant + activation capture on ~128 experts, no full-container read; a full build (only after both falsifiers clear) is the container-design plan-scale -- ~363 GB read plus a comparable write, hours of I/O, engine-idle gated, the same class of cost as the existing mixed int4/int2 container build. Kernel work (group-scale decode format) is a new matmul_i2/fmt==3 variant, not yet scoped in engineer-days.

MEASURED UPDATE (2026-07-15, commit 16bbffc): the offline replay above IS the falsifier this entry's own FIRST stage called for, already run -- see the prediction field and the layout-grid measurement for the full numbers. Verdict: decisively nearer +21% than +49% (this entry's own groupwise tier measures +28.0-31.4% at the anchored ~10 GB/s bandwidth); the +49% scenario is refuted at measured disk bandwidth. Caveats carried forward from the replay itself, not resolved by it: (1) the non-disk compute floor C=0.36 s/token is HELD FIXED in this sensitivity conversion -- real expert-matmul time plausibly shrinks with smaller int2 payloads and may grow with M-dependent latency effects, neither modeled; (2) the constant-bandwidth conversion (t=C+B_miss/BW) is optimistic relative to the measured K6-matrix disk fits, which were SUBLINEAR (b=0.34-0.51, the offline math-verdict record Study 1) -- a sublinear real fit would shade every tok/s delta above toward the low end of its bracket; (3) quality is NOT adjudicated by this replay -- it assumes the repaired quantizer's 0.380 rel-Frobenius (measured on synthetic Gaussian weights) transfers to real expert weights and clears the quality gates, which remains this entry's SECOND and THIRD falsifier stages, untouched by anything above. Status is unchanged (mechanism/performance/shipping all still Modeled/Pending/Not-built): this is a validated offline simulation, not a real-engine wall-clock measurement -- the replay's own tok/s numbers are documented as sensitivity-only, B_miss bytes/token is its authoritative output.

entries.name: Variable-rate group quantization (2-bit default + error-promoted 4-bit groups)

regime.context: external-panel proposal, 2026-07-15, not yet built; sibling of m1, promotes sensitive groups to 4-bit instead of a flat group-int2 rate
regime.cache: expert cache; modeled ~2.6 bits/weight average
regime.container: proposed: 2-bit default per group + promoted 4-bit groups by activation-output error, ~2.6 bits avg -> ~12-13 MB/expert
regime.backend: CPU/Metal (variable bit-width within one expert is a new format; no existing kernel decodes mixed group bit-widths inside a single expert)

entries.hypothesis: m1's flat group-int2 rate treats every group of one expert identically. If quantization sensitivity varies MORE across groups within an expert than across whole experts -- i.e. there is more dispersion to exploit at group granularity than expert-quant-error-saliency already measured flat (0.88-0.92 relative Frobenius across all 19,200 experts, all layers, all routing mass) -- then promoting only the sensitive minority of groups to 4-bit recovers most of int4's quality at closer to int2's size.
entries.prediction: 2-bit default + promote sensitive groups to 4-bit by activation-output error -> ~2.6 bits/weight average -> ~12-13 MB/expert (vs int4's 18.9153 MB, m1's ~10.1-10.7 MB flat-group-int2). Modeled decode ~2.0 tok/s, with a better quality margin than m1's flat rate because the promoted sensitive groups keep int4 fidelity.

measurements.display: ~2.6 bits/weight average (2-bit groups + a promoted 4-bit minority) -> ~12-13 MB/expert, between m1's flat ~10.1-10.7 MB int2 tier and int4's 18.9153 MB.
measurements.source: external-panel proposal, 2026-07-15

measurements.display: FALSIFIER: quantize every 4th group of the same 128 sampled experts used in m1's falsifier (stratified early/mid/late), measure group-level activation-output-error dispersion, and compare it against expert-quant-error-saliency's own whole-expert dispersion (measured flat at 0.88-0.92 relative Frobenius across all 19,200 experts). If group-level dispersion is not SUBSTANTIALLY larger than that already-measured whole-expert dispersion, the entire premise of variable-rate allocation (some groups are more damageable than others, even though whole experts aren't) fails on this container the same way expert-level saliency-by-frequency and saliency-by-error both already failed (expert-quant-error-saliency; what-doesnt-work #47) -- kill the format rather than build a promotion allocator for a signal that isn't there.
measurements.source: external-panel proposal, 2026-07-15; dispersion baseline performance-theory.json expert-quant-error-saliency

measurements.display: Counterfactual rate-cache value V_e (= B_miss(expert at int4) - B_miss(expert at repaired int2), one-at-a-time byte-LRU replays summed over all 3 traces, 2,000 sampled experts across 40/layer x 50 demotable layers, pins frozen at the all-int4 usage fill; 411/2,000 candidates never appear in any trace, V_e=0 exactly) is statistically ORTHOGONAL to the greedy error-based demotion ranking this file's error-based allocators use (-err_int2, the same ranking expert-quant-error-saliency's allocate_bit_budget.py depends on and the same class of signal this entry's own group-promotion falsifier proposes at group granularity): Spearman -0.0028, Pearson 0.0024 -- effectively zero relationship in either direction. Operating-point stability Spearman(V at all-int4 fill, V at manifest fill) = 0.9441 -- V_e itself is a stable quantity across fill states, it simply carries no information correlated with the error-based ranking.
measurements.source: the new-math replay results Task 3; rate-frontier-values.csv, rate-frontier-summary.json (commit 0af7371)

measurements.unit: % miss-byte Pareto improvement at K=1000, <=0.1% extra distortion (PROVISIONAL)
measurements.display: PROVISIONAL (see caveat below -- the distortion axis rests on an invalidated instrument): matched-distortion Pareto sweep (K demotions from the 2,000-expert sample; epsilon = allowed Sigma-err excess over the greedy set's Sigma-err-minimal K-set; the sweep saturates at epsilon=0.1%) shows a cache-value-aware K-set beating the greedy error-ranked K-set (141/500 and 501/1000 overlap respectively) by +2.08% miss bytes at K=500 (25% of sample) and +2.62% at K=1000 (50%), both at <=0.1% extra distortion BY THE err_int2 INSTRUMENT. One-at-a-time V_e marginals are additive: Sigma(V_e) predicts the replayed K-set delta within +0.66% (K=500) / +1.25% (K=1000), so a full V-aware allocator can reuse these one-at-a-time values directly rather than needing a combinatorial re-solve. B_all-int4 = 1,459.22 GB (3 traces); B_greedy = 1,436.59 GB (K=500), 1,412.93 GB (K=1000). Kill line for this frontier (Spearman>0.95 AND Pareto<2%, i.e. 'the error ranking is already good enough, keep the greedy allocator') is NOT met -- rankings are orthogonal AND the Pareto gain exceeds 2% -- so a cache-aware allocation dimension survives as worth folding in, PROVISIONALLY, pending the caveat below.
measurements.source: the new-math replay results Task 3 Pareto table (commit 0af7371)

measurements.display: HARD CAVEAT, unresolved, and the reason the Pareto figures above are marked PROVISIONAL rather than Confirmed: the 'matched distortion' axis of every number above is measured BY THE err_int2 INSTRUMENT, which performance-theory.json's expert-quant-error-saliency entry has already invalidated (defective qmax=1 ternary-behavior quantizer, floor 0.868 vs 0.343 Lloyd-Max-optimal rel-Frobenius). This study measures the CACHE side of the Pareto face validly (V_e is a real byte-LRU counterfactual, not derived from the error instrument), but the DISTORTION side inherits the same invalidated-without-validation status as every other err_int2-based number in this file. Re-run c/tools/optimize_rate_cache_frontier.py with an activation-output error column d_e (||W4x - W2x|| / ||W4x|| on representative activations, the same standard expert-quant-error-saliency's own notes already require of any lossy-adjacent change) once the quantizer is repaired, before treating the Pareto numbers as actionable.
measurements.source: the new-math replay results Task 3 interpretation; cross-ref expert-quant-error-saliency (commit 0af7371)

entries.notes:
CHEAP FALSIFIER (centerpiece): quantize every 4th group of the 128 experts from m1's stratified sample at both 2-bit and 4-bit, measure per-group activation-output error, and compare the SPREAD of that per-group distribution against expert-quant-error-saliency's already-measured whole-expert spread (flat at 0.88-0.92 -- the same flatness that already killed frequency-based and error-based whole-expert saliency, what-doesnt-work #47 and expert-quant-error-saliency). If group-level dispersion is not substantially wider than that, variable-rate allocation is chasing a signal this container has already been shown not to have at coarser granularity, and the format should be killed before an allocator is built for it. Group-level dispersion being wider than whole-expert dispersion is plausible even if whole-expert dispersion is flat (averaging across a whole expert's worth of weight rows can cancel exactly the kind of localized sensitivity a per-group measurement would reveal), but that is a hypothesis this falsifier tests, not an assumption this entry is allowed to carry into a build. Cost estimate: the falsifier reuses m1's 128-expert sample (marginal cost over m1's own falsifier is small, mostly the every-4th-group bookkeeping); a full build additionally requires a new per-group-bit-width allocator (allocate_bit_budget.py's per-expert greedy demotion, extended to per-group) and a new mixed-bit-width-within-an-expert decode kernel, neither of which exists today -- scope this as strictly larger than m1's kernel work, not yet estimated in engineer-days pending the falsifier's outcome.

COUNTERFACTUAL RATE-CACHE VALUE UPDATE (2026-07-15, commit 0af7371, new-math offline study, c/tools/optimize_rate_cache_frontier.py): tested this file's standing error-based demotion ranking (the same -err_int2 greedy signal expert-quant-error-saliency's allocate_bit_budget.py uses, and the same class of signal this entry's own group-promotion falsifier proposes at group granularity) against a directly-measured counterfactual cache value V_e per expert (one-at-a-time byte-LRU replay swap, int4 vs. repaired int2, 2,000 sampled experts) -- the two rankings are statistically orthogonal (Spearman -0.003), and a cache-value-aware K-set beats the greedy error-ranked K-set by +2.1-2.6% miss bytes at matched (by-instrument) distortion. This PARETO GAIN IS MARKED PROVISIONAL, not confirmed: the distortion axis rests entirely on the same invalidated err_int2 instrument expert-quant-error-saliency already flags, so the finding must be re-run with an activation-output error d_e once the quantizer is repaired before it can justify any actual allocation change. What IS solid regardless of the instrument: the CACHE side (V_e, a real byte-LRU counterfactual) is orthogonal to the error ranking, which is itself informative -- an error-only promotion signal, whether per-group as m2 proposes or per-expert as already shipped, is leaving a measurable cache-value signal on the table, whatever the eventual distortion metric turns out to say. The kill line for the counterfactual-allocator idea itself (Spearman>0.95 AND Pareto<2%) is NOT met, so a cache-aware allocation dimension survives as a candidate to fold in alongside (not instead of) m2's own error-based group promotion -- gated on the same distortion-instrument repair m2's own falsifier already depends on.

entries.name: Split-bitplane int4 streaming (high-plane-first, GEMV-overlapped)

regime.context: external-panel proposal, 2026-07-15, not yet built; latency-only lever, no fidelity change (EXACT bit-decomposition of the shipped int4 codes, not a requantization)
regime.cache: expert cache unchanged (same hit rate, same total bytes/expert)
regime.container: proposed lossless repack of the existing int4 container: each expert's int4 integer code q4 (0-15) split as q4 = 4*q_high + q_low into two 2-bit planes, both planes stored contiguously per expert so the high plane can be read first; same total bytes as today's int4, same existing per-row/group float scale applies to the reconstructed q4 unchanged
regime.backend: CPU/Metal (streamed high-plane-first read + GEMV-overlap of the low-plane arrival; new read/decode path, no quantization change, no requant decision)

entries.hypothesis: Today's expert_load reads one coalesced ~19 MB block per expert (gate/up/down contiguous, the container-design plan) and waits for the whole block before compute starts. Splitting each expert's int4 integer code EXACTLY as q4 = 4*q_high + q_low (a base-4 positional split of the existing 4-bit code into a high 2-bit plane and a low 2-bit plane -- lossless, no approximation, full int4 fidelity preserved once both planes are read) and streaming the high plane first lets the GEMV against q_high begin while q_low is still arriving over the PIPE workers, overlapping part of the disk-bound miss term with compute that would otherwise wait for it -- same total bytes, same fidelity, latency-only.
entries.prediction: Modeled 15-30% decode improvement, i.e. hiding 1/3 to 1/2 of the ~0.30-0.31 s/token non-compute (disk-bound) term -- the gap between the settled 1.42-1.58 tok/s warm-band average (~0.66 s/token) and the measured ~0.36-0.38 s/token non-disk compute floor (docs/roadmap-daily-driver.md).

measurements.display: Modeled 15-30% decode gain from hiding 1/3-1/2 of the ~0.30-0.31 s/token non-compute term (0.66 s/token settled average minus the ~0.36 s/token non-disk floor).
measurements.source: external-panel proposal, 2026-07-15; floor/average figures docs/roadmap-daily-driver.md, README.md

measurements.display: CORRECTION PER EXTERNAL REVIEW (round 2) to an earlier overstatement of this entry's cost: split-bitplane streaming is a LOSSLESS REPACK of the existing int4 integer codes (q4 = 4*q_high + q_low), NOT a requantization -- no FP8 source re-read, no new scale-fitting, no requant error-minimization decision, unlike m1/m2's format changes. The cheap test is therefore an IN-MEMORY bitplane split on CURRENTLY-LOADED/resident experts (no disk read beyond what the engine already does normally, no full-container touch) -- cheaper than treating this as container-rebuild work. A full ON-DISK relayout (writing both planes contiguously per expert so a real streaming read can fetch high-then-low without an in-memory split step) is needed only AFTER the cheap in-memory microbench already shows a win, and even then it is mechanically simpler than the mixed-precision container build (the container-design plan) -- a deterministic bit-shuffle of already-decided int4 codes, not a per-expert quantization decision -- though it remains a real I/O pass of similar byte volume (read ~363 GB, write ~363 GB).
measurements.source: Reviewer qualification, 2026-07-15 (round 2); layout facts the container-design plan, the prefill-I/O study Section 3

measurements.display: Two cautions named explicitly rather than left implicit (per external review, round 2): (1) NOT byte-exact -- computing two separate GEMVs (against q_high then q_low) and summing changes floating-point accumulation order vs one GEMV against the combined code, which can fork output at the rounding level; this is the SAME CLASS of kernel-family rounding variance this file already accepts elsewhere (metal-prefill-attention-kernel-gate-2, dsa-sparse-indexer) under the standing user ruling ('pure = any faithful forward of unmodified weights'), not a new correctness bug, but must be disclosed rather than assumed away. (2) the SECOND GEMV (against q_low once it arrives) may itself eat the overlap this scheme is trying to buy -- if computing against q_low after it lands takes long enough, it can consume the latency hidden by starting early against q_high, which is exactly why the falsifier below measures net of the second GEMV, not just the raw hiding fraction.
measurements.source: Reviewer qualification, 2026-07-15 (round 2)

entries.notes: FALSIFIER: a one-layer forced-8-miss microbench (8 experts guaranteed to miss; per the repack correction above, an IN-MEMORY bitplane split on those 8 experts' already-loaded int4 codes is sufficient for this first probe -- no on-disk relayout needed yet) measuring exactly how much of the low-plane arrival is hidden behind the high-plane GEMV in practice, net of the SECOND GEMV this scheme requires and net of submission/dispatch overhead for two command buffers instead of one (both named as explicit cautions above). Kill unless >=25% of miss latency is hidden net of these costs -- the modeled 15-30% range already carries a margin, and the 25% bar sits deliberately inside that range so the microbench has to clear a real hurdle, not just show a nonzero effect. COST ESTIMATE (revised per the repack correction above): the falsifier microbench is cheap (one layer, 8 experts, an in-memory bit-split of already-loaded codes, no disk I/O beyond normal operation). A full ON-DISK relayout is needed only if the microbench wins, and only then: read ~363 GB, write a new ~363 GB high/low-contiguous layout, hours of I/O, engine-idle gated -- similar BYTE VOLUME to the container-design plan's mixed-precision build but mechanically simpler to implement (a deterministic repack of already-decided codes, not a per-expert quantization decision). This is strictly additive to that container's own cost if both ship (two container variants to maintain), or could in principle be folded into one relayout pass alongside m1/m2's group-int2 tier -- not scoped here. The two named cautions (non-byte-exactness, second-GEMV overlap-eating) were not priced into the original 15-30% estimate and are now load-bearing parts of whether this clears its own bar.

entries.name: Fused eight-expert-layer MoE kernel (single routed-MoE dispatch per layer)

regime.context: external-panel proposal, 2026-07-15, not yet built; targets the ~0.36-0.38 s/token non-disk compute floor directly (docs/roadmap-daily-driver.md)
regime.cache: n/a (compute-side lever, independent of hit rate)

entries.hypothesis: what-works #30 measured 44% gpu-wall-vs-kernel overhead on the expert dispatch path -- the same overhead metal4-moe-submission (batched dispatch, +2.05% median) and persistent-metal-state (+0.00%) each partially attacked without eliminating. Combined with m1's 2-bit tier (higher hit rate, not more compute), modeled 2.7-3.2 tok/s -- the panel's own combined-lever number, not independently re-derived here; both this entry's floor claim and the combined figure are gated on the falsifier below, and a1 alone should be confirmed before stacking claims with m1 (the stack-level promote-bar discipline already applied to metal4-moe-submission/persistent-metal-state, meta-lessons #27). NOTE: this 2.7-3.2 tok/s combines only a1+m1; it is narrower than, and should not be conflated with, the full-stack scenario table recorded in topp-adaptive-expert-routing's notes (which additionally folds in overlap and bandwidth/thermal effects from a2/p3/m3/p2).

The literature caution above (6.5-12.9% measured for a simpler fusion on M4) means this falsifier should be run with real skepticism -- if that pattern transfers, this entry's 19-31% floor claim is likely to land closer to single digits, which would still combine with m1 but not reach the stated 2.7-3.2 tok/s ceiling. Cost estimate: this is new Metal kernel engineering (one large fused kernel replacing ~5 dispatch stages, threadgroup-memory scratch management, the router's top-8 select folded in) -- meaningfully larger than metal4-moe-submission's batching-only change or persistent-metal-state's lifecycle work, both of which reused existing per-stage kernels; not yet estimated in engineer-days, but the 10k-iteration one-layer microbench itself is cheap (no full-model run, no disk I/O) and should be built and run before scoping the full per-layer integration.

entries.name: Route-known arrival-order MoE overlap (async miss reads at router time)

regime.context: external-panel proposal, 2026-07-15, not yet built; formalizes docs/roadmap-daily-driver.md Step 5 ('Arrival-order MoE overlap'), never implemented as its own falsifiable entry
regime.cache: expert cache, existing LRU+pin (same hit rate as today -- exact routing, no prediction)
regime.backend: CPU/Metal (async miss reads into GPU-visible slabs at router time; resident experts launch immediately; reduction at end)

entries.hypothesis: Once the router has selected a token's top-8 experts (EXACT routing, not a prediction), the resident ones can start compute immediately while the misses are read asynchronously into GPU-visible slabs, submitted per-readiness rather than waiting for the whole layer's block to land, with the weighted accumulation reduced at the end. Because routing is already known (not guessed), this is distinct from both killed PILOT variants (pilot-k6-router-lookahead-prefetch, pilot-salvage-prefetch-aware-eviction-veto -- both predicted which experts a FUTURE layer would need, and paid for wrong guesses / cache churn) and from the killed CPU-tail (heterogeneous-cpu-gpu-moe-tail -- ran the miss tail on CPU, competing with Metal for unified-memory bandwidth at the measured ~66% hit rate). a2 predicts nothing and wastes zero bytes; the only open question is how much of the already-known miss latency actually overlaps with already-known resident compute.
entries.prediction: Overlap ceiling = max(compute floor, miss term) = max(0.36, 0.30) = 0.36 s/token vs today's ~0.66 s/token sum -- the same ~2.8 tok/s ceiling roadmap-daily-driver.md and README.md already record for 100%-hit / perfect overlap. Modeled realistic 1.75-2.1 tok/s at 30-60% hiding of the ~0.30 s miss term (0.36+0.30*0.7=0.57 s/tok -> 1.75 tok/s at 30% hiding; 0.36+0.30*0.4=0.48 s/tok -> 2.08 tok/s at 60% hiding).

measurements.display: Ceiling max(0.36,0.30)=0.36 s/token (the same ~2.8 tok/s 100%-hit ceiling already on record) vs today's ~0.66 s/token; realistic 1.75-2.1 tok/s at 30-60% hiding of the ~0.30 s miss term. Evidence of headroom already on record: roadmap-daily-driver.md Step 5 notes blocked-pipe time is approximately equal to the disk timer today, i.e. essentially none of the current miss latency is hidden behind compute yet.
measurements.source: external-panel proposal, 2026-07-15; headroom note docs/roadmap-daily-driver.md Step 5; floor/miss split docs/roadmap-daily-driver.md, README.md

measurements.display: Distinct from killed PILOT (pilot-k6-router-lookahead-prefetch: predicted a FUTURE layer's experts, ~19% wasted/late loads, net -6.96% median; pilot-salvage-prefetch-aware-eviction-veto: -26.32% median, zero hit-rate change) -- a2 has no prediction and zero wasted bytes by construction, acting only on the CURRENT layer's already-resolved routing. Also distinct from the killed CPU-tail (heterogeneous-cpu-gpu-moe-tail: -6.3% to -12.6% from unified-memory bandwidth contention with Metal at ~66% hit rate) -- a2 keeps everything on GPU; the miss reads are async I/O, not CPU compute competing for the same bus.

measurements.display: MEASURED (2026-07-15, commit 16bbffc): the same replay that scored m1/c1 found P(M<=2)=65% on today's layout (52% of decode calls stall on exactly 1-2 missed 18.9 MB reads, the regime this entry's arrival-order overlap targets directly), rising to 85% under the repaired-tier-plus-byte-accounting scenario (layout D) -- and its own 'D3' conclusion names arrival-order overlap 'the one GPU program justified at the current layout,' ahead of the fused all-hit path (c1), which the same measurement found premature today. PRIORITY UPGRADE per this measurement: this entry should be treated as immediately actionable, not gated on any capacity change landing first -- unlike c1, which the same replay shows needs the capacity change (m1/m2) before it pays off.

measurements.unit: ms exposed_stall (grouped-CPU-MoE production shape, ILI_STALL_TRACE=1, fixture-validated)
measurements.display: ILI_STALL_TRACE instrumentation (commit 499048d, merged 243e512) added per-layer decode timestamps (route-ready, resident-expert compute start/finish, per-miss read issue+completion, reduction-start) directly to moe(), deriving exposed_stall_ms = max(0, last_miss_complete - resident_finish) -- exactly the gap this entry's own 5-layer falsifier (below) called for. Fixture-validated end to end (compiled zero-warning, run against a tiny numpy fixture in both blocking and PIPE=1 modes, confirmed a true no-op with tracing off -- byte-identical stdout vs the unpatched engine): the M5 Max GENERATED engine's grouped-CPU-MoE production shape (gen_m5max_engine.py's chained patch_m5max_grouped_cpu_moe.py + fix_m5max_grouped_build.py -- the shape that actually ships) drains ALL missed-expert reads behind an upfront gather-then-compute barrier BEFORE resident-expert compute starts, so exposed_stall_ms is ~0 regardless of PIPE. This is a STRUCTURAL finding, not a favorable-baseline one: exposed stall is ~0 TODAY because the code SERIALIZES (every miss is read and drained before any compute begins), not because compute/read overlap is already being captured -- the opposite of what a near-zero exposed-stall number suggests read naively. Applied directly to a pristine (non-grouped) glm.c, per-expert hit/miss granularity and a genuine reduction_start timestamp are preserved; under the grouped rewrite, reduction_start is honestly reported unavailable (-1) rather than fabricated.

measurements.display: VERDICT: FAIL (the a2-falsifier verdict, commit c627421; registered the a2-overlap falsifier registration, commit 15c7a7b). Measured on epoch-05 source with env-gated no-op instrumentation (output parity proven: argmax-hash 1b4e675e identical trace-off), real model, trace_1 snapshot, RAM_GB=2/CPU/PIPE-off, 75 step-0 layers; 5 representative layers (3,21,40,59,77) directly timestamped for nmiss/stall_ms/stagger/compute: median overlap ceiling 16.0% (per-layer range 9.8-28.3%), aggregate compute/stall ratio 0.276 -- per-expert compute (~0.9ms/layer) is ~3.6x smaller than expert-streaming stall (~3.3ms/layer), so at most ~16% of the block is hideable behind compute. FAILS by the registered rule's second clause: completions ARE staggered (0.6-5.8ms stagger measured, confirming the arrival-order half of this entry's own hypothesis), but per-expert compute is too small to hide meaningful latency -- compute scarcity, not batch-arrival, decided the FAIL. The previously-modeled ~1.9x-class overlap ceiling assumed the ~47% exposed stall (Stage-1 baseline, p2-m5-gpu-tensor-path-probe entry) was fully hideable; it is not. REVISED realistic ceiling: ~1.2x (a possible ~10-20% optimization), not the ~1.9x this entry's own prediction modeled -- and building even that ~1.2x needs its own RAM_GB=114 confirmation (this falsifier ran compute-starved at RAM_GB=2/0%-hit) plus its own cost/benefit registration; the grand overlap win is refuted regardless of RAM tier, since the compute<<stall structure is regime-robust per the VERDICT's own caveat.
