entries.notes:
MECHANISM UPDATE (2026-07-15, commit 499048d/243e512): the stall-trace instrumentation this entry's own falsifier called for now exists and confirms, on the shape that actually ships (the M5 Max grouped-CPU-MoE production path), that exposed stall is ~0 today ONLY because the code gathers every missed expert's bytes into one contiguous buffer and waits for all of them before resident-expert compute (and the reduction) ever start -- a hard upfront barrier, not an emergent property of good scheduling. This changes what 'implementing a2' means in practice: it is not a matter of submitting already-known-async reads slightly earlier against a pipeline that already overlaps some of the time, it is restructuring the gather-then-compute barrier itself into per-readiness submission (resident experts compute while misses are still in flight, reduction waits only on the slowest miss) -- a larger structural rewrite than the scheduling-tuning framing this entry's cost estimate (1-2 weeks, docs/roadmap-daily-driver.md Step 5) may have implied. This measurement was taken on a tiny synthetic fixture with a fully-controlled trace (validating the INSTRUMENT and the STRUCTURAL fact about the shipped code path), not a real 19,200-expert production decode run -- it does not substitute for the 5-layer real-engine timestamp falsifier below, which still needs to run to measure actual overlap headroom under real miss latencies and real GPU/SSD concurrency effects; it does confirm that falsifier's first kill-condition ('the existing pipeline already overlaps >70% of miss latency') is FALSE on the shipped grouped shape, the opposite extreme from a wall that would leave nothing for a2 to capture.

FALSIFIER: instrument 5 real layers with four timestamps each -- route-ready (router output available), first-kernel-start (resident-expert compute begins), last-miss-completion (slowest async read lands), reduction-start (weighted accumulation begins) -- and compute actual overlap directly from the gaps. Kill if either: the existing pipeline already overlaps >70% of miss latency behind compute (little headroom left to buy, contradicting the 'blocked-pipe ~ disk timer' note above), OR GPU/SSD concurrency effects inflate the measured layer wall beyond the modeled ceiling (async reads and resident-expert Metal dispatch contending for unified-memory bandwidth the way the CPU-tail scheme did, via a different path -- the distinctness argument above is a hypothesis about WHERE the contention lives, not a guarantee there is none). Cost estimate: this is a genuine scheduling/plumbing change (async read submission at router time instead of at block-boundary, GPU-visible slab management, per-readiness submission, end-of-layer reduction) -- docs/roadmap-daily-driver.md's own Step 5 estimate was 1-2 weeks; the 5-layer instrumentation falsifier itself is cheap (timestamps only, no new I/O path) and should run before committing to that estimate.

MEASURED UPDATE (2026-07-15, commit 16bbffc): the same-day byte-aware replay that scored m1/c1 prices this entry's regime directly -- P(M<=2)=65% today (see the real-replay measurement) means the majority of decode calls are exactly the 1-2-miss case this entry's overlap targets, and the replay's own conclusion ranks this as the one GPU program justified at today's layout, ahead of c1's fused path (which needs the capacity change first). This raises this entry's priority relative to c1 specifically, but does not substitute for the 5-layer timestamp falsifier above -- P(M<=2) prices how often the opportunity exists, not how much of it a real implementation could actually overlap.

FALSIFIER VERDICT: FAIL (2026-07-17, commit c627421, registered the a2-overlap falsifier registration commit 15c7a7b) -- see the measurement above for the full per-layer table. This refutes the ~1.9x-class overlap ceiling this entry's own prediction modeled: the 1.9x figure assumed the ~47% exposed stall (Stage-1 baseline, p2-m5-gpu-tensor-path-probe entry) was fully hideable behind compute, which the direct 5-layer measurement shows is a miscalculation -- per-expert compute (~0.9ms/layer) is ~3.6x smaller than expert-streaming stall (~3.3ms/layer). The registered rule's arrival-order clause DID hold (completions are staggered 0.6-5.8ms, not a simultaneous batch); it was the compute-scarcity clause that killed it. NEXT per the VERDICT's own roadmap note: reassess -> compression (a bigger byte-reduction lever) becomes the priority, gated on the self-fork determinism blocker (a-rope-threadgroup-race entry, this file) -- and the CONFIRMED causal result (Stage-2 v4, p2-m5-gpu-tensor-path-probe entry) that streaming delay drives decode latency still stands independently of this ceiling revision.

entries.name: Depth-axis within-token prefetch (predict layer L+1/L+2 experts from layer L state)

regime.context: Trace-first offline falsifier, 2026-07-18/19 (pre-registered gate: live implementation proceeds only if this offline sim says net-positive at plausible accuracy), then adversarially reviewed by an external LLM reviewer on 2026-07-19; reuses c/bench-m5max/a2-falsifier/a2_layers.jsonl -- the SAME per-layer timeline a2-route-known-arrival-order-overlap captured -- for a DIFFERENT mechanism (cross-layer/depth-axis prediction, not same-layer arrival-order overlap)
regime.cache: RAM_GB=2/0%-hit trace regime (the only per-layer timing data that exists at this granularity); daily-driver ~65%-hit regime untested and flagged as likely to SHRINK the modeled upside, not just rescale it (see notes)
regime.batch_S: S=1 decode (per-token depth-axis lookahead; one hop L->L+1, or two hops L->L+1->L+2)
regime.container: int4 (per-expert bytes 18,915,328 exactly, matching the project-wide b_e=18.9153MB constant used in the t_token model)
regime.backend: CPU (grouped-CPU-MoE upfront-barrier shape, unmodified/not touched); the simulator models a HYPOTHETICAL NVMe prefetch path offline -- no engine change, no GPU touched

entries.hypothesis: Using layer L's own gate/hidden state to predict layer L+1's (or L+1 and L+2's) routed top-8-of-256 experts, and issuing NVMe reads for the guessed set during layer L's own wall-clock window, can convert some fraction of L+1's real misses into pre-resident hits, hiding load stall -- net of predictor compute cost, false-read bandwidth cost (every guessed expert is fetched whether the guess is right or wrong), and contention with L's own demand reads on the shared NVMe pipe. Distinct from a2 (a2-route-known-arrival-order-overlap: same-layer, exact-routing overlap, FALSIFIED at ~16% median ceiling) and from the killed PILOT variants (pilot-k6-router-lookahead-prefetch: decode-time unified-memory contention loss) -- this entry is cross-layer/depth-axis PREDICTION specifically, calibrated against real published accuracy/cost priors (Fate, ACM WWW 2026; LayerScope/LLaPor, ICS '26) rather than an assumed hit-rate, per the deep-research synthesis (docs/deep-research-faster-stronger-smarter-20260718.json).
entries.prediction: Trace-first offline simulator (c/bench-m5max/depth-prefetch/sim_depth_prefetch.py) against the same 225-row (3 decode steps x 75 MoE layers) per-layer timeline a2 captured. Oracle (perfect accuracy, zero predictor cost, single hop) is reported as a BOUND, not a point, per review ruling 1: 1.0847x (pessimistic, 13.5 GB/s device-throughput reference) to 1.3047x (optimistic, ~44 GB/s -- the trace's own implied concurrent bandwidth for demand reads) -- neither bound is strictly correct; the true figure is the unmeasured marginal NVMe service rate for prefetch bytes ADDED on top of demand reads under queue depth and demand-read priority. At the deep-research's calibrated priors (Fate 77-84% one-layer-ahead accuracy, LLaPor 0.12-0.48ms predictor cost), corrected for overlap-given-miss credit (a_eff = a+(1-a)*o, o=0.5): the safe/capped policy (never contends with demand reads) ranges 0.97x-1.08x at the pessimistic bandwidth bound (knife-edge; breakeven predictor cost ~0.34-0.38ms) to 1.12x-1.27x at the optimistic bound (comfortably positive across the whole LLaPor cost range); the naive/aggressive policy (commits to full completion, contends with demand reads) is a decisive 0.40-0.42x (net loss, NEVER breaks even at any accuracy/cost tested) at the pessimistic bound, but 1.08x-1.25x (comfortably positive) at the optimistic bound. depth=2 (extending prediction to L+2) is dominated by depth=1 at every tested point. VERDICT: NO-GO for a live build today; UNRESOLVED-conditional pending the reopen gate (see notes), not archived.

measurements.display: Oracle (a=1.0, predictor_cost=0, depth=1, capped/safe policy) reported as BOUNDS per review ruling 1: pessimistic 1.0847x at the 13.5 GB/s device-throughput reference; optimistic 1.3047x at ~44 GB/s (the trace's own implied concurrent bandwidth, bytes(L)/load_stall_ms(L), which runs 17.1-69.1 GB/s across the 225 sampled rows, median 43.6/mean 44.2). A separate ground-truth reconciliation using each row's OWN exact implied bandwidth (rather than a flat 44.0) reproduces the falsifier registration's originally-cited 1.27x oracle to within 0.6% (1.2784x) -- confirming what that figure assumed: a perfect, free, single-hop predictor restricted to each layer's genuinely idle compute window, converting that window into bytes at the SAME concurrency benefit demand reads already show. Neither bound is strictly correct; true value is the marginal NVMe service rate for ADDED (not replacing) prefetch traffic under queue depth + demand-read priority, unmeasured by this or any existing capture.

measurements.display: Review ruling 4 objected that charging the full top-8 guessed-set transfer as false-read cost overstates waste when accuracy>0 (predicted set P and true set T, both size 8, overlap even on a 'miss'). The benefit-side fix (a_eff = a+(1-a)*o, o='overlap-given-miss', anchored at Fate's own illustrative misprediction example o=0.75) is genuine and shipped. A FIRST implementation ALSO scoped the aggressive policy's contention charge to only the 'waste' (1-a_eff) fraction of the full transfer while leaving frac_landed=1 (always finishes) -- checked against the hard constraint 'imperfect, non-zero-cost prediction cannot beat the perfect, zero-cost oracle,' it FAILED: at bw=13.5, a=0.84, o=0.5, that variant gave depth=1/aggressive a 3.18x speedup, exceeding the a=1.0 capped oracle's 1.08x ceiling. Root cause: you cannot know which of the 8 guesses are 'waste' until the true routing resolves, so you cannot pay for only that portion and still guarantee full completion -- the completion/contention test must stay on the FULL k-expert transfer for both policies. A systematic check across all 2,376 corrected sweep rows (8 policy x depth x bandwidth groups) confirms ZERO cases where an imperfect/costly configuration beats its own zero-cost/perfect-accuracy oracle under the SHIPPED (non-waste-scoped-contention) model.

performance.display: Trace-first offline simulation only (evidence_class offline-simulation throughout). The sign of the verdict now hinges on one unresolved bandwidth fact -- both the safe and naive policy clear breakeven across the realistic 77-84%/0.12-0.48ms range at ~44 GB/s but are dead-to-knife-edge at the conservative 13.5 GB/s reference. REOPEN GATE (pre-registered, 2026-07-19): (a) cheapest decisive scalar -- measure real Metal predictor p95 latency under CONCURRENT layer compute; >0.38ms/layer closes the case permanently at the pessimistic bandwidth bound regardless of accuracy. (b) Full decision -- a capped-policy A/B microbench on a ~65%-hit trace with demand-priority I/O (demand reads must not be slowed by prefetch), the only way to directly measure the marginal-bandwidth question rather than bound it. (c) The ~65%-hit daily-driver regime is expected to SHRINK this trace's 0%-hit upside, not just rescale it: fewer misses per layer to convert; resident (already-cached) correct guesses are free hits regardless of prediction, so this 0%-hit trace's credited benefit is likely inflated; and cache-pollution from wrong guesses evicting genuine LRU hits is a cost this 0%-hit trace cannot see at all (nothing productive to evict when the cache is already empty). If reopened, replay actual residency (byte-LRU at RAM_GB=114) rather than scaling these numbers algebraically. (d) depth=2 stays dominated/closed independent of (a)-(c).

entries.notes:
Reuses a2's own captured per-layer timeline (a2-route-known-arrival-order-overlap, c/bench-m5max/a2-falsifier/a2_layers.jsonl) for a genuinely different mechanism: a2 asked whether compute on ALREADY-KNOWN-routed resident experts can hide load stall WITHIN a layer (FALSIFIED, ~16% median ceiling); this entry asks whether PREDICTING a FUTURE layer's routing from the current layer's state and prefetching ahead can hide stall ACROSS layers. Calibrated accuracy/cost priors are drawn from docs/deep-research-faster-stronger-smarter-20260718.json (Fate ACM WWW 2026: 78.79% measured one-layer decode-prefetch accuracy, 76.94-83.99% ablation range; LayerScope/LLaPor ICS '26: 0.5-2.8MB/layer micro-predictor, 0.12-0.48ms/forward-pass, floor never below 80% but validated only to 128 experts) -- ActiveFlow's 95%/80%/120% figures are explicitly excluded as priors per that same synthesis (dense-operator channel sparsity, not MoE routing; its multi-layer-lookahead claim failed verification 0-3). The Stage-1 baseline 47.0%-exposed-stall measurement (c/bench-m5max/stage1-calibration/) and Stage-2 v4's CONFIRMED causal result (added expert-read delay increases decode latency, c/bench-m5max/stage2-v4/VERDICT.txt) are the standing ground truth this entry's byte/bandwidth model is built consistently with, not a re-litigation of either.

EXTERNAL ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (2026-07-19): reviewed the first trace-first pass and issued four rulings. Ruling 1 (bandwidths must be bounds, not a point) and ruling 4 (byte-charging must credit partial overlap on a 'miss,' not treat every non-exact guess as a total loss) required an actual simulator correction, re-run and verified (2,376-row sweep, 216-row breakeven grid). A literal reading of ruling 4 that ALSO scoped the contention/cost charge to only the 'wasted' bytes was implemented, checked against a hard internal-consistency constraint, found to violate it (documented above as a rejected sub-variant/negative result), and NOT shipped -- the wall-clock arithmetic keeps the full-transfer completion test from the original model; only the benefit side (a_eff) and reporting (byte-weighted precision/recall, both of which collapse algebraically to a_eff since |P|=|T|=8 and every expert is the same byte size) were corrected. Full derivation, the rejected variant's exact numbers, and the reopen gate are in the depth-prefetch trace verdict section 0; sections 1-8 of that document are the original (superseded but preserved) trace-first pass.

entries.hypothesis: Every calibrated-model prediction in this batch's kernel-side entries (a1, a4, and by extension m1-m3's decode-throughput combination) assumes SOME achievable GPU rate without having independently measured the M5 Max's actual primitives on iliria's actual shapes. An M4 study (arXiv 2606.12765) found FP8 tensor ops effectively emulated rather than routed through genuine tensor-core paths -- if M5's tensor primitives are similarly wrapper-only for these shapes, every kernel-rewrite entry in this batch is optimistic by construction. This must be measured directly on M5, not assumed from any other chip generation's numbers, including the M4 finding cited here. REVISED PER EXTERNAL REVIEW (round 2): the compute-side tensor-path question is only half of this probe's job -- the disk term feeding every tok/s prediction in this batch also needs to be measured with the same rigor, at the right granularity (see the bandwidth and roofline definitions below), not represented by one borrowed number.
entries.prediction: Compute side: 0-10% improvement if M5's tensor-primitive path turns out to be wrappers over the same scalar/simdgroup rate already calibrated (the DSA Metal-kernel study's R=0.65e12 MAC/s, ~5% of GPU peak, naive one-thread-per-element kernels); 1.5-3x on eligible stages if the tensor path is real on these specific shapes (576xT scores, 6144x2048 expert GEMMs, int4-dequant tiles). Disk side: no point prediction -- this probe's job is to MEASURE the three bandwidth definitions and two rooflines below, which the t_token model (topp-adaptive-expert-routing notes) currently treats as assumed inputs.

measurements.display: M4 study (arXiv 2606.12765) found FP8 tensor ops effectively emulated, not routed through genuine tensor-core paths -- the motivating precedent for why this must be measured on M5, not assumed. This is a caution from a DIFFERENT chip generation, not a prediction for M5; hence this entry's own top-level evidence_class is literature-only rather than calibrated-model -- unlike every other entry in this batch, p2 has no local numeric model of its own yet, only a reason to distrust assuming one.

measurements.display: REVISED PER EXTERNAL REVIEW (round 2): the disk term needs THREE DISTINCT bandwidth definitions, not one 'sustained throughput' figure -- (1) device throughput (raw SSD hardware bandwidth, e.g. today's 13.3 GB/s figure, the prefill-I/O study); (2) read-path throughput including syscall/scatter-gather overhead (device throughput minus the real code path's per-call overhead); (3) EXPOSED critical-path bandwidth = compulsory miss bytes / main-thread storage stall -- the ONLY one of the three that belongs in the tok/s model (BW_exposed in the t_token formula, topp-adaptive-expert-routing notes), since it is specifically the portion NOT already hidden by overlap/pipelining. Swept over 1-16 concurrent reads x {10-20 MB int4, 5-11 MB int2} objects x warm/cold x isolated/with-GPU-load -- the size range spans both today's int4 tier and the int2-family tiers (today's defective 9.458 MB and m1's repaired ~10.1-10.7 MB), and the with-GPU-load condition is what actually tests for the unified-memory bandwidth contention heterogeneous-cpu-gpu-moe-tail already found matters at moderate hit rates.

measurements.display: REVISED PER EXTERNAL REVIEW (round 2): TWO separate rooflines, not one 30-minute soak -- (1) cold first-5-min roofline (peak/burst performance before thermal throttling engages); (2) power-constrained steady-state roofline over 30-60 min, with full telemetry (GPU frequency/power, memory-controller bandwidth, SSD temperature, fan state). ENDPOINT CLAIMS MUST USE THE STEADY-STATE MEDIAN, not the cold/burst number -- every tok/s figure in this batch that feeds the roadmap-target scenario table (topp-adaptive-expert-routing notes) is only as credible as this discipline being followed. A 15% thermal derate (theta_thermal=1.15 in the t_token formula) is the difference between the scenario table's CENTRAL 2.3-2.8 tok/s and its AGGRESSIVE 3.0-3.5 tok/s band.

entries.name: Unified-memory overlap ring (page-aligned GPU-visible slab ring for miss streaming)

regime.context: external-panel proposal, 2026-07-15, not yet built; targets the ~0.30 s/token miss term directly, distinct from a2's arrival-order scheduling change
regime.cache: expert cache, existing LRU+pin (unchanged hit rate -- pure plumbing/latency lever)
regime.backend: CPU/Metal (page-aligned GPU-visible slab ring; event-driven NVMe->GPU handoff; no CPU copies or re-registration)

entries.hypothesis: Today's PIPE worker path (8 threads, expert_load's coalesced preads, the prefill-I/O study / the M5-Max grouped-CPU-MoE study) still involves per-block dispatch and registration overhead on the CPU side of the handoff. A page-aligned ring of GPU-visible slabs, with event-driven NVMe->GPU handoff and no CPU copies or slab re-registration per miss, could shave the fixed overhead per miss without changing the fundamental disk-bandwidth ceiling (13.3 GB/s device throughput, the prefill-I/O study; see p2 for the finer-grained bandwidth breakdown) -- a narrower, more mechanical claim than a2's scheduling-order change.
entries.prediction: Ceiling = the same ~0.30 s/token miss term already established (0.66 s/token settled average minus the ~0.36 s/token non-disk floor); realistic 50-120 ms/token recovered (8-22% of the settled ~0.66 s/token decode time).

measurements.display: Ceiling = the ~0.30 s/token miss term; realistic 50-120 ms/token (8-22% of the ~0.66 s/token settled decode average) recovered by removing per-miss CPU-side overhead (copies, slab re-registration) rather than by improving overlap scheduling (a2's lever) or raw bandwidth (already at 13.3 GB/s device throughput, the prefill-I/O study).
measurements.source: external-panel proposal, 2026-07-15; floor/average figures docs/roadmap-daily-driver.md, README.md; bandwidth ceiling the prefill-I/O study

entries.notes: FALSIFIER: an 8-expert forced-miss microbench (same forced-miss style as a1's and m3's falsifiers) isolating exactly the per-miss CPU-side overhead this entry targets (copy + registration cost, measured directly rather than inferred), extrapolated to a per-token estimate. Kill unless >=40 ms/token is extrapolated from that microbench -- set below the realistic-range floor (50 ms) so the microbench has to clear a real bar rather than merely show a nonzero effect, consistent with how m3's falsifier sets its own bar inside rather than at the edge of its modeled range. Overlaps in scope with a2 (both touch the miss path) but is a narrower, more mechanical claim -- p3 is about removing fixed per-miss overhead on an otherwise-unchanged schedule, a2 is about changing WHEN misses are issued and WHEN resident compute starts relative to them; the two could compose (p3's cheaper per-miss handoff makes a2's overlap scheduling more effective) or could be found to target the same few tens of milliseconds, in which case only the larger of the two should ship. Cost estimate: a page-aligned GPU-visible slab ring with event-driven handoff is a moderate rewrite of the existing PIPE worker registration path (the persistent-Metal-state lifecycle work, docs/m5max-route-trace-cache-sim.md, is the closest existing precedent for keeping GPU-visible state alive without per-call re-registration) -- smaller in scope than a1's full kernel fusion or a2's scheduling change, but not yet estimated in engineer-days; the 8-expert forced-miss microbench is cheap and should run first.

entries.name: Two-path decode state machine (GPU-driven fast path for all-resident layers)

regime.context: external-panel proposal, 2026-07-15, not yet built; explains why persistent-state/batching measured ~nothing, and specifies the capacity change that would justify building this
regime.cache: expert cache; h^8 all-resident-layer argument at h=0.65 (today) vs h=0.82/0.90 (post-2-bit-tier scenarios)
regime.container: int4 today; mixed int4/int2 in the h=0.82/0.90 scenarios this entry reasons about
regime.backend: CPU/Metal (proposed GPU-driven fast path for layers where all 8 routed experts are already resident, falling back to today's mixed path otherwise)

entries.hypothesis: persistent-metal-state (+0.00%, null result) and continuous-batching-2-stream-decode (falsified, NO-GO) both tried to build fast-path/batching machinery on top of TODAY's cache capacity. The h^8 argument: treating each of a layer's 8 routed experts as an independent hit/miss draw at hit rate h, the probability ALL 8 are resident (an 'all-resident layer', eligible for a GPU-only fast path with no miss-handling logic at all) is h^8. At h=0.65 (today, the settled 64.7-66.1% hit-rate band), h^8=0.65^8=0.032, i.e. only ~2.4 of the 75 main MoE layers/token are all-resident (0.032*75) -- there is almost nothing for a fast path to accelerate today, which is exactly why persistent-state and batching measured ~nothing: they built infrastructure for a regime that barely exists yet. At h=0.82 (a post-2-bit-tier scenario, e.g. m1's modeled hit rate), h^8=0.82^8=0.204, ~15 layers/token all-resident; at h=0.90, h^8=0.430, ~32 layers/token. A GPU-driven two-path state machine (fast path for all-resident layers, today's mixed path otherwise) is justified only AFTER a capacity change moves h materially above today's ~0.65.
entries.prediction: Build only if >=15% of layers measure all-hit at the relevant hit rate, or if the mixed path is shown to measurably overlap with the fast path (running both concurrently doesn't just serialize behind whichever is slower). At h=0.65 today: ~3.2% of layers all-hit (2.4/75), well below the 15% bar -- NOT justified today. At h=0.82 (m1's modeled scenario): ~20.4% of layers all-hit (15.3/75), clearing the bar. At h=0.90: ~43% (32.3/75). REVISED PER EXTERNAL REVIEW (round 2): these h^8 figures assume independence across a layer's 8 routed experts and are a starting hypothesis, not the falsifier itself -- see the fuller distributional falsifier below, which measures the real per-layer miss structure directly instead of assuming independence.

measurements.display: h=0.65 (today): h^8=0.032 -> ~2.4 of 75 layers/token all-resident (~3.2%). h=0.82 (m1 scenario): h^8=0.204 -> ~15.3 layers (~20.4%). h=0.90: h^8=0.430 -> ~32.3 layers (~43%). Build bar set at >=15% all-hit layers, which the h=0.65 regime misses by a wide margin (explaining persistent-metal-state's +0.00% and continuous-batching-2-stream-decode's NO-GO -- both built fast-path-adjacent machinery for a regime with almost no all-resident layers to exploit) and which h=0.82+ scenarios clear.
measurements.source: external-panel proposal, 2026-07-15; hit-rate band performance-theory.json kv-slot-allocation-economics, persistent-metal-state; layer count the offline math-verdict record ('75 MoE layers x 256 experts, top-8 routed')

measurements.display: REVIEWER QUALIFICATION (round 1): the h^8 math above assumes INDEPENDENCE across a layer's 8 routed experts -- treating each as an unrelated coin flip at rate h. Real hits are almost certainly CORRELATED, because the resident set is not a uniform random h-fraction of each layer's 256 experts: it is a frequency-pinned hot store (static pin + per-layer LRU, docs/m5max-route-trace-cache-sim.md) that concentrates on whichever experts are most likely to be routed together. If a token's routing correlates with the pin/LRU's own frequency ranking (plausible -- both are downstream of the same routing distribution), a token that hits on one of its 8 routed experts in a layer is MORE likely than h to hit on the others too, meaning all-hit layers are likely MORE common than h^8 predicts, at every value of h including today's 0.65 -- not just in the post-tier scenarios.
measurements.source: Reviewer qualification, 2026-07-15 (round 1)

measurements.display: FALSIFIER, REVISED PER EXTERNAL REVIEW (round 2), replacing a simpler 'all-hit frequency' measurement: extract, per layer-step, (a) the FULL per-layer miss-count distribution P(M=0..8) (M = number of the 8 routed experts that miss, not just the M=0 all-hit case); (b) bytes-missed per layer-step, not just miss count -- heterogeneous expert sizes matter here exactly as they do for m1's byte-capacity point; (c) hit-indicator pairwise correlations across the 8 routed experts -- MEASURING, not assuming, the correlation structure the independence qualification above raises; (d) max miss-completion time per layer -- the slowest of up to 8 concurrent miss reads, which sets when a simple wait-for-all-misses fallback path can actually proceed; (e) consecutive-all-hit RUN lengths, not just isolated all-hit frequency -- a GPU fast-path state machine's value depends on staying in the fast path across a RUN of consecutive all-hit layers without switching overhead, so the run-length distribution is what actually PRICES whether building the state machine is worth it. MOST OF THIS ALREADY EXISTS: c/tools/simulate_bytes_cache.py's --miss-structure flag (committed 2026-07-15, commit 16bbffc) computes (a) directly (pm_all/pm_steady), (b) directly (bytes_by_m with mean/p50/p90/p99), (c) directly (mean_pairwise_r_pooled and mean_pairwise_r_stratified via per-layer np.corrcoef on the 8-wide hit-flag vector), and (e) directly (run_hist, frac_layers_in_runs_ge2/ge3) -- this is a RUN, not a BUILD, for (a)/(b)/(c)/(e). Only (d), max miss-completion TIME per layer, is not yet computed by that tool (it is a byte/count accounting simulator, not a latency/concurrency timing model) -- a small addition, or a separate estimate from the per-miss-latency figures elsewhere in this file (the prefill-I/O study), is still needed for that one piece.
measurements.source: Reviewer qualification, 2026-07-15 (round 2); tooling c/tools/simulate_bytes_cache.py (committed, commit 16bbffc), docs/m5max-route-trace-cache-sim.md

measurements.display: MEASURED (2026-07-15, commit 16bbffc): on today's layout (A), P(M=0)=0.133-0.138 vs h^8=0.081-0.090 -- all-hit layers measured 1.5-1.65x MORE common than the independence prediction, confirming the correlated-hits qualification directly (mean pairwise hit-indicator correlation, stratified by layer, r~+0.02 -- small but enough to move P(M=0) about 10% above even the layer-stratified independence prediction). Consecutive-all-hit run coverage (the run-length statistic that actually prices the state machine): only 13.8% of layer-calls are all-hit and only 5.6% sit in runs >=2 -- BELOW this entry's own >=15% build bar. Under the repaired-tier + byte-budget-accounting scenario (layout D), all-hit share rises to 31.9% and runs>=2 coverage to 20.2% -- clearing the bar. The replay's own conclusion (its 'D3' question): the fused all-hit path is premature TODAY and pays off only after (or together with) the capacity change -- exactly this entry's own gating logic, now measured rather than assumed. NOTE the measured hit rate this replay used (h=0.731-0.741 on layout A) is HIGHER than the ~0.65 this entry's own hypothesis text uses (sourced from the K6-matrix live-engine capture, a different trace/config) -- both figures are measured, from different sources, and the discrepancy is flagged (see m1's prediction field) rather than silently resolved; recomputing h^8 at h=0.74 gives 0.0888, matching this replay's own h^8=0.081-0.090 range, so the 'h^8=0.032' / '~2.4 layers' figures in this entry's own hypothesis/prediction fields are the K6-matrix-calibrated numbers, not this replay's.
measurements.source: the offline-replay results (commit 16bbffc, produced by c/tools/simulate_bytes_cache.py against routes-baseline.bin, routes-coding.bin, routes-shotgun.bin; validated within 0.4pp of the offline math-verdict record Study 1's own anchors)

measurements.display: Layer-capacity water-filling (Mattson exact hit curves + DP, same 2,550-unit/34-per-layer budget the engine uses today, pins frozen): the DP-optimal per-layer allocation beats the uniform ecap by only +2.7-3.4% in-sample and +1.9-2.4% pooled-deployable (DP fit on one trace, evaluated on the other two) whole-trace miss bytes, across baseline/coding/shotgun. Mean-only DP allocation ranges 13-107 units/layer (vs. today's flat 34) -- confirms, from a different angle than the h^8/run-length falsifier above, that the LAYER-ALLOCATION dimension of capacity is nearly as flat a lever as the eviction-POLICY dimension pilot-salvage-prefetch-aware-eviction-veto already closed.

measurements.unit: % CVaR95 spanned across the full lambda dial
measurements.display: CVaR_0.95 tail-risk variant (pooled per-call miss-byte distributions, f_l = E[bytes_l] + lambda*CVaR95(bytes_l), same 2,550-unit budget, lambda in {0, 0.5, 1, 2}): capacity does flow toward the early band as lambda rises (uniform 850 early-band units -> 1007 at lambda=0 -> 1084 at lambda=0.5) but the whole dial spans only -2.1%..+1.3% in mean miss bytes and about -1.2%..+0.06% in CVaR95 -- a near-flat, largely degenerate plateau. At lambda=2 the -1.18% CVaR gain (vs. uniform) costs +1.29% mean, and vs. the mean-only optimum the same CVaR point costs +3.5% expected miss bytes -- a poor trade. Verdict: marginal-standalone.

measurements.display: The 7-8-miss early-layer tail calls this capacity dial targets are real (132-151 MB/call) but per-layer LRU capacity is the wrong lever for them: lossless compression of the (already-protected) early int4 experts compresses at the same ~0.7379 ratio as everything else (n1-lossless-entropy-coded-experts) and attacks the same tail bytes without spending any LRU capacity -- a compressed 8-miss call reads ~111 MB instead of 151 MB even before any cache-capacity change.
measurements.source: the new-math replay results Task 2a interpretation; cross-ref n1-lossless-entropy-coded-experts (commit 0af7371)

entries.notes:
FIRST FALSIFIER (ahead of the repaired-container falsifier below, and requiring NO repaired container at all): the full distributional falsifier spec above (per-layer P(M=0..8), bytes-missed, hit-indicator correlations, max miss-completion time, consecutive-all-hit run lengths) is measurable OFFLINE TODAY, on the CURRENT int4 container (layout A in c/tools/simulate_bytes_cache.py's own scheme), from the existing route traces (routes-baseline.bin, routes-coding.bin, routes-shotgun.bin) plus the current pin/LRU set -- via that tool's --miss-structure flag, which already implements four of the five statistics (see the falsifier-spec measurement above for exactly which). This requires no 2-bit tier, no repaired quantizer, and no engine time -- strictly cheaper than the second falsifier, and it should run first since it tests the independence ASSUMPTION itself (which the h=0.82/0.90 projections above also silently make), not only the projected regime; the run-length statistic in particular is what turns 'is there an all-hit layer' into 'is there enough of a RUN of them to amortize a state machine's switching cost,' which a single frequency number cannot answer. SECOND FALSIFIER (as originally scoped, confirms the scenario once a repaired tier exists): run the same --miss-structure analysis against layouts C/D/E in the same tool (the repaired per-row and groupwise tiers), and build the two-path state machine only if >=15% of layers measure all-hit (or the run-length distribution shows economically meaningful runs) OR the mixed path is shown to overlap with the fast path rather than serialize behind it. Cost estimate: the first (distributional) falsifier is now mostly a matter of RUNNING already-built tooling against already-committed traces (minutes to an hour), with one small gap to fill (max miss-completion time per layer is not yet computed by simulate_bytes_cache.py and needs either a small addition to it or a separate latency estimate). The second falsifier requires the 2-bit tier to exist first (m1/m2's own cost applies) but reuses the same tool once that tier's manifest exists. The state machine itself, if justified, is a moderate decode-loop change (a fast dispatch path conditioned on a per-layer all-hit check, falling back to today's path) -- smaller than a1's kernel fusion, larger than a config toggle; not yet estimated in engineer-days pending both falsifiers.

MEASURED UPDATE (2026-07-15, commit 16bbffc): the FIRST falsifier above (offline, no repaired container needed) has already been run against today's layout -- see the real-replay measurement for the full numbers. It empirically confirms the round-1 correlated-hits qualification (all-hit layers ARE more common than h^8 predicts, by 1.5-1.65x) and empirically answers the round-2 run-length falsifier (only 5.6% of layer-calls sit in all-hit runs of length >=2 today, below the 15% build bar; 20.2% under a repaired-tier-plus-byte-accounting scenario, clearing it). The one gap the tooling still doesn't fill -- max miss-completion time per layer -- remains open. Status unchanged: this is a real, validated offline simulation confirming the entry's own gating logic (don't build the state machine before the capacity change), not a build decision or a status change.

WATER-FILLING UPDATE (2026-07-15, commit 0af7371, new-math offline study, c/tools/variable_size_cache_oracle.py): tested directly whether reallocating the SAME 2,550-unit budget non-uniformly across the 75 layers (Mattson exact hit curves + DP, uniform int4, pins frozen) beats today's flat 34-slots/layer ecap -- it does, but only marginally (+2.7-3.4% in-sample, +1.9-2.4% pooled-deployable miss bytes), confirming from a different angle that per-layer capacity is nearly as flat a lever as the eviction-POLICY dimension pilot-salvage-prefetch-aware-eviction-veto already closed: capacity-vs-reuse-distance is the wall along both the policy axis and the inter-layer allocation axis. The CVaR_0.95 tail-risk variant partially confirms the intuitive appeal of protecting the early band (capacity does flow there as lambda rises) but the entire lambda dial moves CVaR95 by only about 1.2 points on a largely degenerate plateau -- not worth a standalone capacity-allocation feature. The tail phenomenon this was aimed at (7-8-miss early-layer calls reading 132-151 MB) is real, but the better-targeted fix is lossless compression of the early int4 experts (n1-lossless-entropy-coded-experts), which attacks the same tail bytes without spending any LRU capacity at all.

entries.name: Immutable transcript sidecar (content-addressed tool-blob store + prefix-hash KV snapshots)

regime.context: external-panel proposal, 2026-07-15, not yet built; composes with context-diet-trimming (text-shrinking) and serve-prefix-kv-reuse-delta-prefill (KV reuse) rather than replacing either
regime.cache: content-addressed tool-blob sidecar + prefix-hash-keyed KV snapshots (proposed, alongside .ili_kv's existing prefix-KV slots)
regime.backend: n/a (harness-level: content-addressed storage + KV snapshotting, pre-/around-engine)

entries.hypothesis: context-diet-trimming already shrinks what the CLIENT sends by truncating old tool output to a frozen excerpt (opt-in, default off). c2 goes further: store tool-call blobs content-addressed (so identical tool output across turns/sessions is byte-shared, not re-sent or re-rendered), keep stable excerpts (the SAME frozen-at-first-trim invariant context-diet-trimming already proved with two unit tests), and snapshot KV state keyed by a PREFIX HASH rather than only by session/slot -- so a session that revisits a previously-seen prefix (not just its own immediately-preceding turn) can resume from a KV snapshot instead of re-prefilling, extending serve-prefix-kv-reuse-delta-prefill's per-session delta-only prefill into a cross-session, content-addressed KV cache.
entries.prediction: Modeled t'/t ~ 0.45*r^2 + 0.55*r, where r is the fraction of a session's prompt bytes that are NOT hash-hit (r=1 is today's no-reuse case, r->0 is full reuse) -- giving 2.3-4.5x TTFT at r=0.55-0.32 (a plausible range for agent-harness transcripts with meaningful tool-output repetition), or 1.8-3.1x under DSA (DSA's own crossover already captures part of the same long-context TTFT benefit, per dsa-metal-kernel-design-study's crossover tables, so the two levers partially overlap rather than stack multiplicatively).

measurements.display: t'/t ~ 0.45*r^2 + 0.55*r (r = non-hash-hit fraction of prompt bytes) -> 2.3-4.5x TTFT at r=0.55-0.32; 1.8-3.1x under DSA (dsa-metal-kernel-design-study's crossover already captures part of the same long-context TTFT benefit, so the two levers partially overlap rather than stack multiplicatively).

measurements.display: Builds on context-diet-trimming's proven frozen-excerpt invariant (two committed unit tests: test_trimmed_message_is_frozen_and_stable_as_history_grows, test_frozen_form_survives_a_mid_session_budget_change, the context-diet analysis) and extends serve-prefix-kv-reuse-delta-prefill's per-session .ili_kv prefix matching to a cross-session, content-addressed store. Also interacts with kv-slot-allocation-economics: prefix-hash-keyed snapshots are additional RAM/disk state competing with the same expert-cache budget that entry's economics already price -- a slot-like cost this entry's own cost estimate must account for.
measurements.source: performance-theory.json context-diet-trimming, serve-prefix-kv-reuse-delta-prefill, kv-slot-allocation-economics

entries.notes: FALSIFIER: replay 20 representative agent tasks through the sidecar+snapshot design with a PREREGISTERED success margin (decided before the replay runs, not fit to the result afterward -- the same discipline this file already applies to A/B promotion bars), and kill auto-replacement of today's per-session-only KV reuse if measured task success drops on the replay, even if TTFT improves. This is a correctness/safety falsifier, not just a speed one: content-addressed cross-session reuse and prefix-hash-keyed snapshot resumption are both NEW ways for a session to read state that did not originate in its own immediately-preceding turn -- exactly the class of bug the prefix-stability invariant (context-diet-trimming, the context-diet analysis) was built to prevent within a single session -- extending reuse ACROSS sessions multiplies the ways a stale or wrongly-matched snapshot could silently corrupt a transcript, so a success-rate regression on the replay is disqualifying regardless of any TTFT win. Cost estimate: content-addressed blob storage (hash-keyed, dedup on write) is a moderate storage-layer addition; prefix-hash-keyed KV snapshotting is the larger piece (a snapshot/restore format for KV state, a hash-keyed index matching prefixes ACROSS sessions rather than the current single-slot-per-session model, and an eviction/staleness policy for the snapshot store) -- meaningfully bigger than context-diet-trimming's pure text-side change, in the same rough class as building a new cache tier alongside the existing expert cache and KV slots; not yet estimated in engineer-days. The 20-task replay itself is cheap relative to the storage-layer build and should run against a PROTOTYPE snapshot store before the full design is built out.

entries.hypothesis: The shipped int4 integer codes (4-bit fields, values 0-15) are stored raw/unpacked; if their empirical symbol distribution carries less than 4 bits/weight of true entropy, a lossless entropy coder recovers that gap as a smaller on-disk/in-RAM footprint per expert -- cutting miss bytes with EXACT (bit-identical) weight recovery, unlike every lossy tier elsewhere in this file (m1/m2/tiered-int4-int2-mixed-precision-container). Whether the win is realizable depends on WHICH consumption mode is used and whether a real decoder can meet that mode's throughput requirement -- corrected below from an earlier 'mode-3-or-nothing' framing, which understated pipelined mode-1 and overstated mode-3's simplicity.

measurements.display: H(Q) global mean 2.9401 bits/weight (p50 2.9148, range 2.6700-3.0242) across 768 tensors (256 experts stratified early/mid/late x gate/up/down, seed 20260715). measurements.unit: % change in whole-trace B_miss vs int4-raw byte-LRU baseline
measurements.display: Applying the measured 0.7379 rANS@64KB ratio to whole-trace byte-LRU B_miss at UNCHANGED hit rate: baseline 479.69 GB -> 353.98 GB (-26.2%); coding 483.53 GB -> 356.82 GB (-26.2%); shotgun 496.00 GB -> 366.02 GB (-26.2%). measurements.display: CORRECTED MODE TAXONOMY (external review round; supersedes an earlier 'mode-3-or-nothing' framing that conflated serial and pipelined mode-1 and mischaracterized mode-3 as a bare miss-path-only budget): MODE-1 (serial disk-decompress-then-expand-into-RAM, one pass fully completes before the next starts) needs strict B_d > B_s/(1-rho) -- at rho=0.7379 that is 38.2 GB/s at B_s=10 GB/s / 50.7 GB/s at B_s=13.3 GB/s -- DEAD at any realistic CPU decompressor. MODE-1.5 (pipelined: read compressed blocks and expand them CONCURRENTLY with the next block's read, not serially) relaxes the requirement to B_d > B_s (plus a small fixed startup/tail cost) -- i.e. only ~10-14 GB/s sustained decoder output, matching rather than multiplying the read bandwidth -- ALIVE, and a materially easier bar than the old single-mode framing implied. MODE-3 (decode fused directly into the dequant loop that already walks every nibble, no separate expansion pass) remains the PREFERRED mode: besides the ~26% byte cut, it also buys capacity (more experts resident in RAM if storage stays compressed there too) and may cut GEMV memory traffic (smaller resident footprint touched per matmul) -- benefits mode-1/1.5 do not offer. Its budget of 80.7ns/4KB (13.3GB/s miss path) / 2.68ns/4KB (400GB/s DRAM path) is MISS-PATH-ONLY as originally stated; the FULL direct-decode condition for the capacity-boosting variant must additionally net out a decode TAX PAID ON EVERY HIT (not just misses, since RAM-resident copies would also be compressed) against the BENEFIT of a lower miss probability from that same higher resident capacity -- this net condition is not yet modeled with real numbers and is an open falsifier item, not merely a restatement of the miss-path budget. MODE-4 (RAM stays compressed, expanded before every consumed expert regardless of hit/miss -- the entry's earlier 'mode 2') adds an 11.35 GB/token expansion tax (600 expert-uses/token x 18.9153 MB) needing 17-34 GB/s sustained expansion at 1.5-3.0 tok/s -- DEAD, unchanged by this correction.
measurements.source: the new-math replay results Task 1 break-even table and 'per consumption mode' section (commit 0af7371); mode taxonomy correction: Reviewer qualification, 2026-07-15 (external review round)

measurements.display: The choice of entropy coder is an open EMPIRICAL RACE, not settled by the ratio table above: candidates are interleaved rANS (best measured ratio, 0.7379), canonical Huffman+LUT decode (0.7524, likely faster to decode via table lookup), FSE/tANS (a table-driven rANS variant, not yet measured here), and a branchless bitplane-exception format (not yet measured here). The WINNER should be whichever gives the lowest END-TO-END GEMV TIME once fused into mode-3's dequant loop, not whichever has the smallest container -- rANS's ~1.5-percentage-point ratio edge over Huffman (0.7379 vs 0.7524) may lose to Huffman's likely-simpler/faster table-driven decode once actual per-tile decode latency is measured on hardware. This race has not been run; it is a precondition for mode-3, not a detail to settle after choosing rANS by default.
measurements.source: Reviewer qualification, 2026-07-15 (external review round); ratio baseline the new-math replay results Task 1

measurements.unit: compressed/raw byte ratio at 4KB blocks (rANS, median expert)
measurements.display: The 0.7379 headline ratio was measured at 64KB blocks, which decide DISK storage/transfer size -- but mode-3's in-kernel tile decoder must decode ROW-INDEPENDENTLY (a GEMV consumes weight rows one at a time and cannot wait for a whole 64KB block spanning many rows), and gate/up rows (~3KB) and down rows (~1KB) are both far smaller than 64KB. The census's own 4KB-block figure is the closest available proxy for this: rANS@4KB median-expert ratio is 0.7442 (vs 0.7379 at 64KB) -- about 0.6 percentage points worse, from per-block index/table overhead amortizing over fewer bytes, even though entropy itself barely changes with tile size (H tile 4KB 2.9350 bits/weight vs H global 2.9401). True ROW-level (1-3KB) ratios were NOT directly measured by this census and are expected to be worse still than the 4KB figure, plus a separate row_offsets random-access index (~24KB/projection, small in aggregate but a real fixed cost) is needed for row-independent access. Mode-3's real feasibility must be evaluated against this ROW-CODED ratio, not the 64KB headline number -- an open measurement gap, not yet closed.
measurements.source: Reviewer qualification, 2026-07-15 (external review round); 4KB/64KB figures the new-math replay results Task 1 raw tables, census-summary.json (commit 0af7371)

measurements.unit: row-coded compressed/raw byte ratio (rANS, 4-way interleaved, best real codec)
measurements.display: CODEC RACE RUN (2026-07-15, the codec-race results): four row-independent (per-row-decodable) reference-C codecs benchmarked on a synthetic corpus calibrated to the census's own per-(band,projection) entropy. Row-coded stored ratio / 1-thread GB/s / 18-thread GB/s: rANS 4-way interleaved 0.7489 / 0.13 / 1.46 (best decode throughput AND second-best ratio); canonical Huffman+wide-LUT 0.7536 / 0.10 / 1.20; tANS/FSE 0.7474 / 0.10 / 1.04 (best ratio, worst throughput); branchless bitplane+exception 1.0022 / 29.29 / 51.12 (an outright EXPANSION -- correctly falls back to raw passthrough on this H~2.9-3.0-bit/weight data, so its ~51 GB/s is really just today's matmul_i4/qt_addrow nibble-unpack cost, included here as the baseline mode-3 decode must beat, not as a competing codec). rANS wins the race outright: best decode throughput at both thread counts (+22% over Huffman, +40% over FSE at 18 threads) AND a ratio within 0.15pp of FSE's best -- confirming n1's own prior framing ('rANS's ratio edge over Huffman may not survive a decode-speed comparison') resolves in rANS's favor on BOTH axes, not by trading one for the other. Row-coding tax vs. the census's 64KB-block headline: row-coded ratios land only 1.0-1.6 percentage points worse (rANS 0.7489 row-coded vs 0.7379 at 64KB) because a SHARED per-projection codebook amortizes table cost to near-zero, smaller than the census's own 4KB-block proxy (0.7442) suggested.
measurements.source: the codec-race results (commits 8731ee3, 9704af7, 8b295f4, merged 3767ab4); c/codec_race.c, c/codec_row_{rans,huff,fse,bitplane}.h

measurements.unit: x too slow vs mode-3's own 13.3GB/s-miss-path decode budget (rANS, best real codec, 18 threads)
measurements.display: FALSIFIED ON CPU, both consumption modes that need a real decoder: MODE-3 (fused in-kernel tile decode) needs 77.3 ns/4KB (rANS's own budget at the 13.3 GB/s miss-path bar) but measures 2,796 ns/4KB at 18 threads -- FAIL by 36.2x (Huffman 45.1x, FSE 50.4x; each codec's own measured ratio implies its own budget, computed the same way for all three). At the harder 400GB/s DRAM-path bar the gap is three orders of magnitude (1,087-1,516x). MODE-1.5 (pipelined disk-decompress, needing only to MATCH read bandwidth ~10-14GB/s, not the tile-fusion budget) is ALSO dead on these three reference-C codecs: 18-thread throughput (1.04-1.46 GB/s) sits roughly 7-13x below its own easier ~10-14GB/s bar -- a smaller shortfall than mode-3's 36-50x, but still definitively short, so both modes are dead pending a non-scalar (SIMD/GPU) decoder. Both verdicts are reference SCALAR C decode only (explicitly out of scope: SIMD/GPU); mode-3's ~35-50x gap is judged too large for plausible SIMD vectorization alone (typically 4-8x for this code class) to close unaided.
measurements.source: the codec-race results 'Mode-3 budget check' table and verdict section

measurements.display: Remaining path, NOT YET RUN: a Metal (GPU) row-decoder probe, launched 2026-07-15 15:33 as one of the day's follow-on builders, is entropy's preregistered last chance before this frontier is considered closed on the CPU verdict above. Neither bar has been evaluated as of this entry; both mode-3 and mode-1.5 stay dead pending this probe's result.

With CPU decode now falsified for both modes, the container target REVERTS from case 5 (+45%) to case D (m1-groupwise-symmetric-int2-tier's own repaired-int2-only tier at byte-budget LRU accounting, +32.6-33.7%) as the pragmatic near-term build target, UNLESS the Metal row-decoder probe above surprises (clears its preregistered budget). measurements.unit: GB/s steady-state GPU decode-only throughput (canonical-Huffman, 16,384-row scale)
measurements.display: METAL ROW-DECODER PROBE RESULT (2026-07-15, the Metal row-decode results; commits e385b5b/04d7044): the preregistered last-chance probe named above HAS NOW RUN. (A) mode-1.5 REVIVED: steady-state canonical-Huffman GPU decode-only throughput is 36.5 GB/s at the default 16,384-row scale (range 36.28-36.58 GB/s across 6 repeated runs) and 61.3 GB/s at 32,768 rows -- 3.6-6.1x over the preregistered >=10 GB/s revival bar, and comfortably clearing the CPU study's own 13.3 GB/s miss-path bandwidth bar too (CPU rANS, the CPU winner, reached only 1.46 GB/s at 18 threads). GPU row-level parallelism (thousands of independent per-row decode threads hiding each other's serial bit-walk latency) succeeds where 18 CPU threads could not. (B) mode-3 STILL DEAD: fused decode-GEMV throughput reaches at most 52.4% of the plain int4-unpack-GEMV baseline (31.7-52.4% across 16,384-row runs, mean 42.1%; 37.4-40.1% at 32,768 rows) -- never reaching the preregistered >=60% GEMV-parity bar. Every decode was verified bit-exact against a CPU reference before any timing number was trusted (16,384/16,384 and 256/256 rows).
measurements.source: the Metal row-decode results (verdict section); c/tests/test_metal_row_decode.mm; commits e385b5b, 04d7044

performance.display: Split verdict as of 2026-07-15: mode-3 remains FALSIFIED on both CPU (36-50x short) and GPU (42.1% mean vs the 60% bar -- see measurement above) -- fused in-kernel decode is dead on this hardware/format regardless of CPU or GPU. mode-1.5 (pipelined disk-decompress + GPU-decode-on-load) is REVIVED: GPU row-parallelism clears both the 10 GB/s preregistered bar and the CPU study's 13.3 GB/s miss-path bar by 3.6-6.1x (36.5-61.3 GB/s measured). mode-1.5 is PROVISIONAL-alive pending a real pipelined disk-read-to-GPU-decode implementation (the probe measured the decode kernel in isolation, not a full pipeline).

shipping.display: Not-built: mode-1.5's GPU decode kernel cleared its preregistered budget (measurement above) but a full disk-read-to-GPU-decode PIPELINE does not exist yet -- that integration is the next falsifier before mode-1.5 ships. mode-3 stays not-built/dead on this format regardless of CPU or GPU.

entries.notes:
BREAK-EVEN IS WHERE THIS FRONTIER IS ACTUALLY DECIDED, not the size number: the ~26% lossless cut clears its kill line comfortably (0.7379 median vs the >0.85-is-dead bar) and is uniform across bands/projections -- H p1-p99 spans only 2.67-3.02 bits, and tile-size/row-scale conditioning buy ~0 extra bits, so there is no headroom for fancier scalar or per-block modeling; real gains beyond ~26% would need vector/context models, which are kernel-hostile. CORRECTED MODE VERDICT (external review; an earlier 'mode-3-or-nothing' framing was too strong): MODE-1 (serial) is dead (needs 38-51 GB/s decompression at today's 10-13.3 GB/s reads). MODE-1.5 (pipelined read+expand, overlapping decode with the NEXT block's read instead of waiting serially) is ALIVE -- it only needs to match read bandwidth (~10-14 GB/s sustained decoder output), a far easier bar, and requires no kernel fusion, only a software-pipelined decompression pass in the existing PIPE workers. MODE-3 (fused in-kernel tile decode) remains PREFERRED because it additionally buys capacity and may cut GEMV memory traffic, but its full feasibility condition is the lower-miss-probability CAPACITY benefit net of a decode TAX PAID ON EVERY HIT (not just misses) -- this net condition is not yet modeled with real numbers, and mode-3's miss-path-only 80.7ns/4KB budget should not be read as the whole story if the capacity-boosting variant (compressed RAM residency) is what gets built. MODE-4 (expand-every-consumed-expert, hit or miss -- the entry's earlier 'mode 2') stays dead, unchanged (11.35 GB/token expansion tax, 17-34 GB/s sustained at 1.5-3.0 tok/s). Verdict for planning: mode-1.5 is the cheap, low-risk, software-only win to pursue first (no kernel change, no format decision beyond picking a codec); mode-3 is the larger prize but is gated on (a) the codec race below and (b) a real hit-tax-vs-capacity-benefit model, not just the miss-path budget.

CODEC RACE: the coder is not simply 'use rANS because it has the best ratio' -- interleaved rANS (0.7379), canonical Huffman+LUT (0.7524, likely faster decode), FSE/tANS, and a branchless bitplane-exception format are all candidates, and the winner should be whichever gives the lowest END-TO-END GEMV TIME once integrated, which has not been measured for any of them yet; rANS's ratio edge over Huffman may not survive a decode-speed comparison. ROW-INDEPENDENT CODING: the 0.7379/64KB figure governs disk storage size, but mode-3 needs ROW-level (gate/up ~3KB, down ~1KB) independent decodability, which the census's own 4KB-vs-64KB comparison (0.7442 vs 0.7379) shows is measurably worse at smaller blocks even though the underlying entropy barely moves -- true row-level ratios (plus a ~24KB/projection row_offsets index) were not directly measured and are the correct number against which to evaluate mode-3, not the 64KB headline. ENGINEERING OVERLAP: mode-3's fused in-kernel tile decode lives in the same territory as a1's fused eight-expert-layer kernel (a1-fused-eight-expert-layer-kernel) -- both touch the per-expert dequant/GEMV inner loop and should be scoped together, not as two independent rewrites of the same code path, if both proceed. STACKS WITH REPAIRED INT2: this format is orthogonal to and stacks with m1's repaired-int2 tier (m1-groupwise-symmetric-int2-tier) -- early layers stay EXACT int4 (now at ~0.74x size via this entry) while the cold/mid-late tier moves to int2. Would flip to Confirmed/performance once (1) the codec race and (2) a mode-3 tile-decode microbench (the same forced-miss style as a1's/m3's falsifiers, measuring real ns/4KB decode cost against the row-coded budget, net of dequant-loop integration overhead and the hit-tax term) both report; mode-1.5 could ship independently and sooner, gated only on the codec race and a software-pipelining implementation, no kernel work required.

CODEC RACE RESULT (2026-07-15, commits 9704af7/8731ee3/8b295f4, merged 3767ab4): the race called for above HAS now run, on reference scalar C decoders, and answers 'no' -- see the four new measurements above. rANS wins the race outright (best ratio-and-speed combination among real compressors) but even the winner fails mode-3's fused-decode budget by 36.2x and mode-1.5's easier read-bandwidth bar by ~7-9x; Huffman and FSE fail both by similar or larger margins. PERFORMANCE FLIPS TO FALSIFIED-ON-CPU as a direct result -- this is a verdict about scalar CPU reference decode specifically (explicitly out of scope: SIMD/GPU), not about the underlying entropy content, which remains real and unchanged (mechanism stays Confirmed). The one surviving path is a Metal GPU row-decoder probe (launched 2026-07-15, preregistered budget: >=10GB/s revives mode-1.5, ~GEMV-parity-class throughput revives mode-3) -- not yet run. Container-planning consequence: the entropy-aware hybrid (case 5, +45-46%, commit 60d33b3) assumed a working entropy decoder and is no longer the default near-term build target; the container reverts to case D (m1's repaired-int2-only tier at byte-budget accounting, +32.6-33.7%) unless the Metal probe surprises. This is a CPU-scoped falsification, not a final kill -- do not read 'not-built/falsified' here as 'entropy coding is dead': the census's ~26% lossless cut (mechanism) is untouched, only the two consumption modes needing a fast CPU decoder are closed off pending the GPU probe.

METAL PROBE RESULT (2026-07-15): the Metal GPU row-decoder probe named above as entropy's preregistered last chance has now run (the Metal row-decode results) -- see the measurement above for the full numbers. Mode-1.5 clears its preregistered revival bar decisively (3.6-6.1x over 10 GB/s); mode-3 does not (42.1% mean vs. the 60% GEMV-parity bar it needed, only narrowing modestly from the CPU study's own ~42% decode-only-vs-unpack ratio, i.e. fusing a GEMV onto the decode does not close the gap). CONTAINER-PLANNING CONSEQUENCE, updated: the entropy-aware case-5 hybrid (+45-46%, commit 60d33b3) required BOTH modes; with mode-1.5 alive and mode-3 dead, case 5 is not simply revived wholesale -- it needs re-evaluation against whichever consumption shape mode-1.5 alone can deliver (pipelined disk-decompress on load, not in-kernel fusion), a smaller claim than case 5's original framing, and depends on the not-yet-built disk-to-GPU pipeline integration. entries.name: Staged intra-expert streaming (dependency-aware two-stage miss read: gate/up before down)

regime.context: external-review proposal, 2026-07-15, not yet built; targets the M<=2-miss regime a2 already prioritizes (P(M<=2)=65% today per the byte-aware replay, commit 16bbffc)
regime.cache: expert cache, existing LRU+pin (unchanged hit rate -- pure read-scheduling lever, no prediction, no wasted bytes)
regime.container: int4 (mechanism-agnostic; composes with m1's repaired tier and n1's entropy coding)
regime.backend: CPU/Metal (two-stage async read per missed expert: gate+up ~12.6MB first, down ~6.3MB concurrently once gate/up compute starts; no format change, no new kernel)

entries.hypothesis: Today's expert_load reads one coalesced ~18.9MB block per missed expert (gate/up/down contiguous) and waits for the WHOLE block before any compute starts. But the down-projection's input (SiLU(gate(x))*up(x)) isn't needed until AFTER the fused gate/up projection and SiLU have already run -- so splitting a missed expert's read into gate+up (~12.6MB) first and down (~6.3MB) streamed concurrently lets compute on gate/up start as soon as its smaller read completes, hiding part of down's read behind gate/up compute. Like a2, this predicts nothing and wastes zero bytes (exact routing, no CPU fallback) -- it only reorders when a single missed expert's own bytes arrive relative to when they're needed.
entries.prediction: Modeled 20-45 ms/token (roughly 3-7% of the settled ~0.66 s/token decode average), realized only on layer-steps where <=2 experts miss (52% of decode calls per the byte-aware replay's P(M<=2)=65% figure, commit 16bbffc) -- above M=2, concurrent-read queue-depth limits how much of this a real NVMe queue can actually overlap.

measurements.display: Modeled 20-45 ms/token (~3-7% of the ~0.66 s/token settled decode average) from overlapping part of a missed expert's down-projection read (~6.3 MB) behind its own gate/up compute (~12.6 MB read first) -- applicable only on the M<=2-miss layer-steps this entry targets (52% of decode calls, P(M<=2)=65% per the same-day byte-aware replay, commit 16bbffc, c1's real-replay measurement). Distinct from a2 (route-known arrival-order overlap, which overlaps ACROSS experts within a layer) -- this entry overlaps WITHIN a single missed expert's own read, and the two mechanisms compose rather than compete.
measurements.source: Reviewer qualification, 2026-07-15 (external review round); byte sizes the container-design plan (18.9153MB/expert, gate/up/down layout); regime frequency the offline-replay results (commit 16bbffc)

measurements.display: Zero prediction, zero wasted bytes, no CPU fallback by construction: EXACT routing (like a2), reading only the SAME bytes today's engine already reads for a missed expert, just reordered/staged and issued as two concurrent async reads instead of one -- distinct from PILOT's speculative loads (pilot-k6-router-lookahead-prefetch, pilot-salvage-prefetch-aware-eviction-veto) and from the CPU-tail scheme's compute contention (heterogeneous-cpu-gpu-moe-tail).
measurements.source: Reviewer qualification, 2026-07-15 (external review round)

entries.notes: FALSIFIER: a forced-miss microbench (1-2 experts guaranteed to miss, same style as a1/m3/p3's forced-miss falsifiers) comparing staged (gate+up read, then down read concurrently with gate/up compute) against today's single coalesced ~18.9MB read, swept over NVMe queue depths 1/2/4 (queue depth is the load-bearing unknown -- above some depth the two reads no longer overlap usefully against a shared device queue). Kill unless the staged path clears >=0.25 ms/missed-layer in isolation OR >=20 ms/token replay-weighted (both bars set inside, not at the edge of, the modeled 20-45ms range, so the microbench has to clear a real hurdle). Overlaps in scope with a2 and p3 (all three touch the miss-read path) but is the narrowest and most mechanical of the three: p3 removes fixed per-miss CPU-side overhead, a2 changes WHEN misses are issued relative to OTHER experts' resident compute, this entry changes how a SINGLE missed expert's own read is staged internally -- the three could compose, and this one is plausibly the cheapest to build first, since it touches only expert_load's own read-issue order, not cross-expert scheduling or slab-registration lifecycle. Cost estimate: 2-4 days (a read-order change plus a dependency-aware compute trigger, no new kernel, no format change) -- cheaper than a2's scheduling rewrite or p3's slab-ring rewrite, reusing the existing gate/up/down contiguous layout. Evidence class Modeled (calibrated estimate only; no local run yet).

entries.name: Symmetry-aligned residual coding (SwiGLU neuron-permutation alignment + prototype/residual entropy coding)

regime.context: external-review proposal, 2026-07-15, not yet built, offline falsifier only; per-layer analysis across the 256 experts of one MoE layer
regime.cache: n/a (storage/compute-structure lever, orthogonal to cache policy and capacity)
regime.batch_S: S=1 decode (compute-sharing mode); n/a for compression-only mode
regime.container: proposed: per-layer neuron-permutation-aligned prototype + entropy-coded per-expert residuals, on top of int4 (or n1's entropy-coded int4); compression-only mode is EXACT/lossless (restores original neuron order, bit-identical numerics); compute-sharing mode changes the arithmetic (shared base GEMV + residual GEMVs) and needs a numerical-equivalence gate
regime.backend: CPU/Metal (proposed: signature-based neuron alignment offline at build time; compression-only mode needs a permutation-undo step in the existing dequant path; compute-sharing mode needs a new shared-base-plus-residual GEMV kernel, not yet built)

entries.hypothesis: A SwiGLU MoE expert's function is exactly invariant under any joint permutation P_e of its intermediate-neuron axis (the same permutation applied to gate's and up's output ROWS and down's input COLUMNS leaves the expert's output identical) -- this is an EXACT structural symmetry, not an approximation, that quantization, caching, and entropy coding (n1) all currently ignore, since each expert is stored/compressed independently in whatever neuron order it happened to train in. If per-expert neuron orders are aligned to a common per-layer prototype (via cheap signatures, e.g. random projections, plus bipartite matching or optimal transport), the 256 experts of a layer should look more alike post-alignment than pre-alignment, making prototype + entropy-coded-residual storage smaller than independently entropy-coding each expert (n1) -- and, in a more aggressive compute-sharing mode, letting the layer evaluate the shared prototype's gate/up GEMVs ONCE instead of per-expert, adding only small residual GEMVs per expert.
entries.prediction: Compression-only mode: no numerical-quality risk (restores original neuron order before use, bit-identical to today's int4 or n1's entropy-coded int4) -- a pure storage-size question, decided by the falsifier below. Compute-sharing mode: modeled work fraction 0.125+r per non-prototype expert (vs. 1.0 today), where r is the residual GEMV's fraction of a full expert's arithmetic -- e.g. r=0.30 gives ~38% less expert arithmetic in the upside case (an UPSIDE-CASE estimate, not a measured one), but requires a new numerical-equivalence gate before any quality claim counts.

measurements.display: The permutation symmetry itself is EXACT, not approximate: for any permutation P_e of the intermediate-neuron axis, applying P_e to gate's and up's output rows and the matching P_e to down's input columns leaves the expert's function bit-for-bit unchanged (a structural property of the SwiGLU form, independent of the specific weight values) -- this is a mathematical claim about the architecture, not something the census or any trace replay measured, and is the load-bearing premise the falsifier below actually tests for EXPLOITABILITY (whether real trained experts are close enough to some common prototype under SOME alignment, not whether the symmetry exists).
measurements.source: Reviewer qualification, 2026-07-15 (external review round); SwiGLU structural argument, not a local measurement

measurements.unit: work fraction (prototype-shared base); +r residual, r assumed 0.30 in the upside case
measurements.display: Compute-sharing mode's modeled per-expert work fraction is 0.125+r (1 shared-prototype gate/up GEMV per layer instead of 8, plus a residual GEMV per expert of relative size r): at r=0.30 (an assumed, not measured, residual density) this is ~0.425 of today's per-expert work, i.e. ~38% less expert arithmetic across the layer's 8 routed experts -- an UPSIDE-CASE estimate contingent on real residual density landing near r=0.30, which the falsifier below measures directly rather than assumes.
measurements.source: Reviewer qualification, 2026-07-15 (external review round)

measurements.display: FALSIFIER (offline, 3 layers x 32-64 experts each, random-projection signatures for cheap neuron-similarity scoring, medoid-based alignment as the bipartite-matching/OT stand-in): measure (a) aligned prototype+residual entropy-coded stored size vs. independently entropy-coding each expert (n1's method, no alignment); (b) residual density (fraction of residual coefficients that are non-negligible after alignment). KILL if aligned stored size is <10% better than independent entropy coding AND residual density >70% (i.e. alignment buys almost nothing and most of each expert survives as an unshared residual -- the symmetry exists but real trained experts aren't close enough to exploit it). PROCEED if aligned exact stored size <0.70x raw int4 (beating n1's own ~0.74x on the SAME lossless-storage axis) OR modeled shared-base compute saving >15% (on the compute-sharing axis).
measurements.source: Reviewer qualification, 2026-07-15 (external review round)

entries.notes: This is the most SPECULATIVE entry in the file's current lossless/structural family (n1, n2) -- the permutation symmetry it exploits is exactly real (a structural property of SwiGLU, not an empirical finding), but whether real trained experts are close enough to a common per-layer prototype for the alignment to pay off is completely untested; the falsifier is offline, cheap (3-5 days, no engine time, no disk I/O beyond reading a handful of layers' experts already read by other census work), and gates BOTH modes before any further scoping. COMPRESSION-ONLY mode is the safe half: it restores original neuron order before use, so it carries the SAME bit-identical-numerics guarantee as n1's entropy coding and composes with it directly (align, then entropy-code the aligned residuals -- potentially stacking with, not replacing, n1's ~0.74x). COMPUTE-SHARING mode is the aggressive half: it changes the actual arithmetic (a shared per-layer base GEMV plus per-expert residual GEMVs instead of 8 independent full GEMVs) and absolutely requires a numerical-equivalence gate (activation-output error vs. today's exact int4, the same standard expert-quant-error-saliency's notes already require of any lossy-adjacent change) before any compute-saving claim counts as more than modeled. Relationship to other entries: shares its offline-falsifier-first discipline with m1/m2/n2; if compression-only mode proceeds, it most naturally stacks with n1 (align first, entropy-code second) rather than replacing it; if compute-sharing mode proceeds, it is a new GEMV kernel family, comparable in scope to a1's fused-layer kernel but orthogonal to it (a1 fuses DISPATCH across 8 experts, this entry would fuse ARITHMETIC across 8 experts via shared structure) -- the two could in principle compose into one kernel, not scoped here. Cite: this is the only entry in the file that exploits an EXACT structural symmetry ignored by quantization (which treats each expert's weights independently), caching (which treats each expert as an opaque indivisible blob), and entropy coding (n1, which compresses each expert's SYMBOL DISTRIBUTION independently) alike -- all three existing levers operate per-expert-independently; this is the first proposal in this file to look ACROSS experts within a layer structurally.

entries.name: Mixed-format (int4/int2) Metal MoE block-dispatch hazard

regime.context: Code-review-found P0 correctness bug, 2026-07-15 (campaign-log.md 13:06:00 entry); fixed same day in commits 1e6ce96 (c/glm.c) + 665e529 (c/backend_metal.mm), merged 2d9ee7a; applies once the tiered-int4-int2-mixed-precision-container has any int2-demoted experts
regime.cache: n/a (dispatch-format correctness bug, not a cache-policy or capacity lever)
regime.batch_S: any S (the affected block-dispatch path runs on every MoE layer call, prefill and decode alike)
regime.container: mixed int4/int2 (the hazard is INERT on a pure-int4 or pure-int2 container; it only triggers when a 64-expert unique-union dispatch block spans both formats)
regime.backend: Metal (GPU routed-expert block dispatch: ili_metal_moe_block[_begin], moe_gemv); CPU path (m5_cpu_moe_subset, M5 Max generated engine) carries the analogous handled[]-mask fix

entries.hypothesis: glm.c's MoE block builder (MB_BUILD) inferred ONE scalar dispatch format (mfmt) from the FIRST expert in a 64-expert unique-union block and never checked the rest. On the tiered int4/int2 mixed-precision container (tiered-int4-int2-mixed-precision-container), where experts are demoted to int2 individually by measured saliency rather than per-layer, a block spanning both formats would submit the WHOLE block under the first expert's inferred format -- ili_metal_moe_block[_begin] has no per-expert format tag, so it would silently decode int2 bytes as int4 nibbles (or vice versa) for every expert in the block that disagreed with the inferred format. Compounding this, moe_gemv's routed-expert kernel had no int2 (fmt==3) branch at all, so any int2 expert reaching the GPU path silently fell back to CPU regardless of the format-inference bug.
entries.prediction: None recorded numerically ahead of the fix -- first identified by code review (campaign-log.md 13:06:00: 'Metal MoE block builder mixed-format hazard... int2-as-int4 silent corruption on mixed container'), which is why gates A/B were run behind ILI_CPU_MOE_ALL=1 (commit 0ce527b) as an interim workaround before any fix existed, specifically so those gates would measure the quantizer rather than a dispatch artifact.

measurements.unit: % worst-case relative log-prob error (pre-fix glm.c, fixed backend)
measurements.display: On the engineered tiny mixed int4/int2 fixture (tiny_mixed_moe_fixture.py: router e_score_correction_bias forces every decode step, every MoE layer, to route to a mix of int4 and int2 experts), reverting to the pre-fix glm.c while keeping the fixed backend reproduced a 6.2% worst-case relative error between CPU-only and Metal-enabled SCORE-mode log-probabilities (test_mixed_format_moe.py's REL_TOL=0.05 tolerance) -- comfortably failing the 5% bar and confirming both that the corruption is real and that this test catches it. Post-fix, the same comparison lands at ~0.1-0.15%, the same float-reassociation-scale band the existing pure-int4 Metal-vs-CPU comparisons already carry -- roughly a 40-60x reduction.
measurements.source: commit 442119f (commit message); c/tests/test_mixed_format_moe.py, c/tests/tiny_mixed_moe_fixture.py

measurements.unit: silent CPU-fallback blocks (of 54 GPU-dispatched per-format sub-blocks)
measurements.display: A temporary counter probe (not committed, per 442119f's own message) instrumented every per-format Metal sub-block across the fixture's decode steps and confirmed the Metal MoE path is genuinely exercised, not silently falling back: 54 GPU blocks dispatched, 0 CPU-fallback blocks, per the P0-kernel-fixes merge commit body (2d9ee7a: 'per-format dispatch verified by counter probe (54 GPU blocks, 0 silent fallbacks)'). ILI_CPU_MOE_ALL=1 was separately confirmed to still reproduce the CPU-only result bit-for-bit -- an explicit-override path, unaffected by this fix.
measurements.source: commit 2d9ee7a (merge commit body); commit 442119f

measurements.display: The new vectorized int2 (fmt==3) branch added to moe_gemv (uchar4 loads, four float4 dot products, mirroring the existing int4 nibble-unpack pattern) matches a CPU reference within 1.1e-6 to 1.4e-6 relative error on synthetic sync/async moe_block coverage in c/tests/test_backend_metal.mm ('moe int2 decode nb=8' / 'moe int2 ragged nb=6') -- the merge commit body states this as 'int2 routed kernel validated 1.1-1.4e-6 vs CPU', the same order of magnitude as the pre-existing int4 coverage's own tolerance, i.e. the new int2 kernel is not a materially less precise addition.

measurements.display: Fix (commit 1e6ce96, c/glm.c): MB_BUILD now takes an explicit target format and only admits experts whose own gate/up/down tensors all agree with it; the surrounding code loops the format space (0..3) for both the async resident submission and the sync missed-expert submission, replacing the old block-level cpu_res/cpu_miss/metal_done booleans with a per-expert handled[] mask so the final CPU loop picks up exactly whatever no per-format sub-block covered (format-inconsistent experts, an unrepresented format, or a sub-block whose GPU call failed) -- never a silent partial fallback. The M5 Max generated engine's grouped/batched CPU path (m5_cpu_moe_subset) carries the same handled[]-mask guarantee (adapted from the old take_res/take_miss booleans); the earlier 'compute missed experts on CPU while the resident Metal block is still in flight' heuristic (m5_defer_resident) was dropped because it does not compose with concurrent per-format resident handles.
measurements.source: commit 1e6ce96 (c/glm.c, c/tools/fix_m5max_grouped_build.py, c/tools/patch_m5max_grouped_cpu_moe.py)
