entries.name: a_rope threadgroup race (RoPE in-place read/write hazard)

regime.context: Code-review-found P0 correctness bug, 2026-07-15 (campaign-log.md 13:06:00 entry: 'a_rope in-place race confirmed... plausibly the run-to-run self-forks'); fixed same day in commit 665e529, merged 2d9ee7a
regime.cache: n/a (attention-kernel synchronization bug, not a cache-policy or capacity lever)
regime.batch_S: any S (a_rope runs on every attention call, prefill and decode alike)
regime.container: int4 (mechanism-agnostic -- a Metal attention-kernel synchronization bug, unrelated to expert quantization format)
regime.backend: Metal (a_rope kernel, c/backend_metal.mm)

entries.hypothesis: a_rope read vv[2j]/vv[2j+1] and wrote vv[j]/vv[hlf+j] in the same thread with no barrier between the read and write phases: for j < hlf/2, another thread j' in {2j,2j+1} WRITES the exact location this thread READS, so correctness relied entirely on an unstated, non-portable assumption that a simdgroup's lanes execute this straight-line code in lockstep -- true on this hardware only because hlf==32==SIMD width and every dispatch happened to use a threadgroup size that is a multiple of 32 (both the natural hlf=32 boundary and the pre-fix code's actual dispatch size of 64 satisfy this incidentally). This was flagged as the leading hypothesis for the project's long-standing, previously-unexplained 'run-to-run Metal self-fork' phenomenon (the DSA Metal-kernel study, docs/roadmap-daily-driver.md: 'the standard multi-threaded Metal config self-forks run-to-run even with frozen usage').
entries.prediction: None recorded numerically ahead of the fix -- first identified by code review (campaign-log.md 13:06:00: 'a_rope in-place race confirmed (line 135, unbarriered interleaved read/split write -- real nondeterminism source, plausibly the run-to-run self-forks)'), flagged as P0 engine work alongside the mixed-format-moe-dispatch-hazard.

measurements.display: run_attn_determinism (c/tests/test_backend_metal.mm), 1000x-repeated identical fused-attention calls at 3 shapes (S=1 pos=0, S=1 pos=37, S=4 pos=12): the barrier-fixed kernel is bit-identical across all 1000 reps at every shape (0 divergences), AND -- run against the ORIGINAL unbarriered kernel on this same hardware -- also 0/1000 divergences at every shape. Per the merge commit body: 'RoPE race real-but-masked on this hardware (0/1000 divergences unfixed...)'. This confirms the race is real per Metal's memory model (the code has no ordering guarantee between the read and write phases) but is MASKED on this specific hardware/dispatch combination, not fixed by luck in this specific patch: the masking depends on the incidental alignment (hlf==32==SIMD width, threadgroup size a multiple of 32) that lets a simdgroup's lockstep execution hide the hazard -- an alignment the pre-fix code never asserted or guaranteed, i.e. fragile by construction (a different dispatch shape or SIMD width could have silently broken it with no code change at all), not a property that code established on purpose.
measurements.source: commit 665e529 (commit message + c/tests/test_backend_metal.mm run_attn_determinism); commit 2d9ee7a merge body

measurements.display: OPEN QUESTION, NOT RESOLVED: fixing this race did not, by itself, confirm or rule out that it was the cause of the project's separately-documented run-to-run Metal self-fork phenomenon (the DSA Metal-kernel study, docs/roadmap-daily-driver.md). The determinism probe's 0/1000 divergences on the UNFIXED kernel (previous measurement) means this specific race was not observed to actually corrupt output on this hardware even before the fix -- consistent with, but not proof of, it being irrelevant to the self-fork mystery. The merge commit body is explicit: 'the self-fork cause lies elsewhere.' The self-fork's real cause remains UNIDENTIFIED as of this entry; read the fix as 'a real, now-closed correctness hazard,' not as 'the self-fork root cause, now found.'
measurements.source: commit 2d9ee7a (merge commit body); Reviewer qualification, 2026-07-15

measurements.display: SELF-FORK BISECT TABLE (2026-07-17), narrowing the open root-cause question above: CPU+REPLAY deterministic (stage2-v4, 20 runs, within-block argmax-hash identity -- see p2-m5-gpu-tensor-path-probe's Stage-2 v4 measurement, commit 5a70329); Metal+REPLAY BIT-IDENTICAL (the Metal-replay probe verdict, commit a7d952b, registered the Metal-replay determinism probe commit 8e8544c: 5 runs x 256/256 tokens, full-logit FNV fingerprints identical across every run at every token, AUTOPIN=0/cap=1 placement PINNED); Metal+free-generation 5/5 DIVERGENT (2026-07-15, pre-existing observation). MECHANISM UPDATE: with a FIXED context, both backends (CPU and Metal) are now shown numerically EXACT under REPLAY -- so divergence requires the CONTEXT ITSELF to fork, ruling out kernel nondeterminism-under-fixed-input as the cause and narrowing the search to generation-path-only mechanisms. PRIME SUSPECT (hypothesis, UNTESTED): run-to-run expert PLACEMENT variability under the daily (non-pinned) config -- AUTOPIN hot-set/LRU state deciding CPU-grouped-vs-Metal execution per expert, whose kernel-family rounding differs -- amplified by token feedback once free generation lets a rounding-level difference change a sampled/argmax token, which changes the context, which changes future routing. The probe that established Metal+REPLAY's exactness ran with placement PINNED (AUTOPIN=0/cap=1); the daily shipped config leaves placement free, which is exactly the variable this hypothesis blames and exactly what pinning removed.
measurements.source: the Metal-replay probe verdict (commit a7d952b); the Metal-replay determinism probe (registration, commit 8e8544c); c/bench-m5max/stage2-v4/VERDICT.txt (commit 5a70329, CPU+REPLAY 20-run determinism)

measurements.display: Fix (commit 665e529, c/backend_metal.mm): dispatch one threadgroup per (row,head) (threadsPerThreadgroup == AROPE/2 == hlf, matching the hazard's natural boundary exactly instead of by incidental multiple-of-32 coincidence) and add a threadgroup_barrier between the load and store phases, so correctness no longer depends on today's incidental alignment. A separate, independent change in the same commit hoists the per-head-redundant pow/cos/sin trig computation (the RoPE angle depends only on (pos,j), never on head, so the old kernel recomputed it identically 64 times per position): a new a_rope_table kernel computes it once per decode step and caches it across layers, invalidated only when pos_base/S/theta change. This trig-table hoist already existed as an M5-Max-only generator patch (gen_m5max_backend.py) and now lives upstream in the shared kernel, so the generator's now-redundant copy was removed.
measurements.source: commit 665e529 (c/backend_metal.mm, c/tools/gen_m5max_backend.py)

performance.display: Null (no throughput number measured for the barrier fix itself; the accompanying trig-table hoist removes a 64x-redundant per-head recomputation but was not separately benchmarked)

shipping.display: Default-on (merged c/backend_metal.mm, 2d9ee7a); no env-var gate, always active

entries.notes:
Do not read this as 'the self-fork mystery solved' -- it explicitly is NOT: the merge commit (2d9ee7a) itself says 'the self-fork cause lies elsewhere,' and the determinism probe found 0/1000 divergences on the UNFIXED kernel too, meaning this race was never observed to actually manifest as visible corruption on this hardware, fixed or not. What IS established: the race is real per the Metal memory model (an unbarriered same-thread read-then-write where another thread can write the read location first is a genuine data race regardless of whether it happens to be masked today); the masking is an incidental, non-portable property of today's dispatch (simdgroup width 32 == hlf, threadgroup size a multiple of 32) rather than a guarantee the code ever asserted; and the fix removes the dependency on that incidental alignment going forward (future dispatch-shape changes, different Apple Silicon SIMD widths, or scheduler changes could otherwise have silently started corrupting output with no code change at all). Found by the same code-review pass that found the mixed-format-moe-dispatch-hazard entry (campaign-log.md 13:06:00); the two are unrelated mechanisms (this is an attention-kernel synchronization bug; the other is a MoE-dispatch format-inference bug) that happened to be found and fixed together as this session's P0 engine work. The run-to-run Metal self-fork phenomenon (the DSA Metal-kernel study, docs/roadmap-daily-driver.md) remains an OPEN, UNIDENTIFIED-root-cause item -- future work chasing it should treat this entry as a ruled-out-by-measurement-on-THIS-hardware candidate, not a confirmed non-cause on all hardware/configurations or a closed investigation.

BISECT UPDATE (2026-07-17): the self-fork search now has a CPU+REPLAY / Metal+REPLAY / Metal+free-generation bisect table (see measurement above) showing both backends are exact under a fixed, replayed context -- the fork requires the context itself to diverge, which redirects the open question toward generation-path placement variability (untested) rather than kernel-execution nondeterminism under fixed input (now ruled out by this bisect). Still NOT resolved: this is a narrower open question, not a confirmed root cause -- treat 'placement variability amplified by token feedback' as the leading untested hypothesis, not a finding.

entries.name: Immutable post-prefill KV snapshot restore (Stage-2 v4 methodology)

regime.context: Process/methodology finding from the Stage-2 v4 registration (2026-07-17, the stage-2 v4 registration, registration commit e876276): replaces live 8K prefill per experimental arm with immutable post-prefill KV snapshot restore, to eliminate prefill-variance noise from paired decode-latency treatment diffs
regime.cache: n/a for the KV-tensor snapshot itself -- orthogonal to the expert LRU/pin cache, which is explicitly NOT persisted and starts fresh every arm

entries.hypothesis: Live 8K prefill per experimental arm (needed to establish the 8K/warm decode condition Stage-2 targets) costs ~3211s/arm all-CPU quadratic attention -- 20 arms would cost ~18h and, more importantly, reintroduces prefill's own run-to-run variance into every paired treatment diff, which is exactly the noise that defeated Stage-2 v2/v3. Serializing the post-prefill KV state ONCE per unique prompt (immutable snapshot, via the same kv_disk_* path serve-mode resume already validated bit-exact) and restoring it in run_replay in place of live prefill -- binding provenance via a sidecar .prov file (source_commit, model dims, prompt hash+count, kv_records; fail-closed on any mismatch) -- should reproduce live-prefill's exact next-token decisions while making every arm's setup phase both fast and byte-identical to every other arm at the same prompt, isolating the treatment (injected read delay) as the only remaining source of paired-diff variance.

source_conflicts.description: Same-day turn-3 serve-gate before/after ratio (1523 s pre-fix / 168.3 s post-fix) printed with two different rounded digits in two committed sources for the identical pair of runs.
source_conflicts.resolution: Direct division of the logged numbers (1523/168.3 = 9.049) rounds to 9.0, matching the internal-findings entry more precisely than this repo's own 9.1. Likely a rounding choice made at different points (9.05 rounds to 9.1 under round-half-up on one significant digit, or 9.0 under truncation/round-to-even), not a different measurement — both sources are citing the same two timings. Not resolved to a single canonical digit in the prose; both are preserved and flagged rather than silently picking one.
